"I can tell you if there is seriousness in the US side to come to a deal and reopen the Strait of Hormuz, everything is now prepared," he added.A US official told the BBC that the US was "in a very strong position with control of the Strait of Hormuz, so we are not in a rush".The MOU between the US and Iran, signed on 18 June, was designed to bring about a ceasefire and at least partly reopen the Strait of Hormuz. The 14-point agreement said Iran would never have a nuclear weapon.
articles.summary: 伊朗外交部长阿巴斯·阿拉格奇表示，伊朗已向美国提出一项协议，将在七天内重新开放霍尔木兹海峡。阿拉格奇在纽约联合国对记者表示，此事「如果满足必要条件」即可实现，并称这些条件已包含在六月签署的谅解备忘录（MOU）之中。他说：「现在选择权在美国手中」，并补充说该方案已通过卡塔尔转交给美国。当被问及伊朗的提议时，一名美国官员对BBC表示，正通过调解人进行积极讨论，包括核问题。本周早些时候，美国总统唐纳德·特朗普威胁要「消灭伊朗伊斯兰共和国」。美国和以色列于2月28日对伊朗发动空袭。伊朗则通过攻击以色列和美国在波斯湾的基地，以及美国的阿拉伯湾盟友进行回应，并封锁了霍尔木兹海峡。战前全球约20%的石油和液化天然气经由该海峡运输，其关闭导致能源价格剧烈波动。这也增加了特朗普寻求结束冲突的压力——尤其是在美国11月国会选举临近之际。阿拉格奇对记者表示：「如果满足必要条件，海峡可以重新开放，正常的海上通行可在七天内恢复。」他没有具体说明伊朗希望美国采取哪些步骤，但补充说：「美国应当采取的行动并非新的，它们都已写在谅解备忘录中。」他补充说：「我可以告诉你，如果美方有诚意达成协议并重新开放霍尔木兹海峡，现在一切都已经准备好了。」一名美国官员对BBC表示，美国「在控制霍尔木兹海峡方面处于非常强势的地位，因此我们并不着急」。美伊之间的这份谅解备忘录于6月18日签署，旨在促成停火并至少部分重新开放霍尔木兹海峡。这份14点协议称，伊朗将永远不拥有核武器。

articles.title: OpenAI bots meddled with multiple US government agency sites
articles.excerpt: OpenAI has acknowledged that it alerted "dozens" of global institutions that their websites may have been meddled with by its AI bots acting improperly.AI agents attempted to get information from "governments, universities, public agencies, and other institutions", including the SEC, Census Bureau and Education Department, the company said. The disclosures come just days after Australian Prime Minister Anthony Albanese announced that OpenAI agents had breached non-public files on the website of its government-run health care scheme, Medicare.Since August, public fears have grown around the potentially serious, even life-threatening, impacts of AI tools falling outside of human control. OpenAI said that some of the data was accessed by AI agents, essentially bots that are designed and trained to operate somewhat autonomously, which were working to find "authoritative sources of public information". But the company noted that some of the bots went beyond that and worked to bypass security measures on websites. When attempting to get information from the Census Bureau, for instance, AI agents used tools reserved for software developers to access it, the company said. OpenAI said all of the government data accessed by bots was public. However, it noted that information that its bots accessed from the SEC, which regulates the US stock market and protects investors, was later published by AI agents on another website. OpenAI says this action was not intended. In other instances that OpenAI disclosed on Friday, its AI agents transferred data when it should not have. Such activity resulted in at least 53 incidents where an OpenAI agent took an image from ChatGPT user activity and transferred it elsewhere.The company said that in each instance of a user image being used and transferred by an AI agent, the user had opted in to allow OpenAI to train models using their data. Nevertheless, OpenAI admitted: "This is not an appropriate use of this data".
articles.summary: OpenAI承认，它已提醒「数十家」全球机构，其网站可能遭到该公司AI机器人的不当干预。该公司表示，AI智能体试图从「政府、大学、公共机构及其他机构」获取信息，其中包括美国证券交易委员会（SEC）、人口普查局和教育部。就在几天前，澳大利亚总理安东尼·阿尔巴尼斯宣布，OpenAI的智能体侵入了其政府运营的医保计划Medicare网站上的非公开文件。自8月以来，公众对AI工具脱离人类控制可能造成严重甚至危及生命的影响愈发担忧。OpenAI称，部分数据确由AI智能体访问——这些智能体本质上是被设计和训练为可在一定程度上自主运行的机器人——它们当时正致力于寻找「权威的公共信息来源」。但该公司指出，一些机器人超出了这一范围，试图绕过网站的安全措施。例如，在试图从人口普查局获取信息时，AI智能体使用了专为软件开发者保留的工具来访问数据，该公司称。OpenAI表示，机器人访问的所有政府数据都是公开的。然而，它指出，其机器人从负责监管美国股市和保护投资者的SEC获取的信息，随后被AI智能体发布在另一个网站上。OpenAI称这一行为并非有意为之。在OpenAI周五披露的其他案例中，其AI智能体在不该传输数据时传输了数据。此类活动至少导致53起事件，其中OpenAI的智能体从ChatGPT用户活动中获取图像并将其传输到其他地方。该公司表示，在每一例用户图像被AI智能体使用并传输的情况中，用户都已选择允许OpenAI使用其数据训练模型。尽管如此，OpenAI承认：「这不是对该数据的适当使用。」

articles.title: Russia targeting 'ordinary life' with attacks on Ukraine's data centres, Zelensky says
articles.excerpt: President Volodymyr Zelensky says Russia has widened its attacks to target Ukraine's data centres and internet providers, seeking to cause maximum disruption for ordinary people."All this affects people's ability to stay connected, study, work," he said.On Friday a Russian drone hit a business centre in the capital Kyiv, killing four people and damaging a data centre. A separate attack killed a 14-year-old boy. Israel's foreign ministry said he was an Israeli citizen.Russia confirmed it had targeted a data centre site, saying it was being used by Ukrainian military intelligence.About 100,000 households in Kyiv and the region suffered internet outages on Wednesday due to strikes.Some firms have already begun moving data from damaged servers to facilities abroad.In the north-western city of Lutsk, electronic information boards at public transport stops were not working on Friday, officials said. The city council said this was "due to damage caused by a Russian attack on data centres in Kyiv".In Friday's social media post, Zelensky wrote: "The Russians are constantly expanding their escalation operation: American and other businesses, data centres, internet providers – for Russia, all ordinary life is simply a target."It is important that the world responds to all of this and that Russia feels the response to its terror."Late on Friday, Zelensky said "additional decisions" had been made at his meeting with Ukraine's top defence and security officials to protect the country's data centres and other critical communications facilities to ensure their continuous operation. Ukraine's Foreign Minister Andrii Sybiha has said that Russia was seeking to disrupt the flow of "life-saving information" by targeting data centres."Rapid alerts about missile and drone threats are essential - they save lives. This is critical civilian infrastructure... It is not a military target.

articles.title: South African white genocide does not exist, new ambassador to US tells BBC
articles.excerpt: South Africa's new ambassador to Washington has a personal reason to challenge Donald Trump's assertion that there is a genocide against white Afrikaners - he is "a born Afrikaner" himself."Is he talking about us?", Roelf Meyer remembers thinking, when he first heard President Trump say it.His response to the US president's claim is blunt. The notion of a mass attack on the white Afrikaner minority in South Africa does not exist, he told the BBC, adding that his identity gave him the legitimacy to say so.Meyer was one of the chief mediators to end white-minority rule known as apartheid in South Africa in the 1990s.

articles.title: Inside the FBI hack: Agents fearful and angry after 'dangerous' data breach
articles.excerpt: Current and former FBI agents have spoken to BBC News of their shock, fear and anger following a hack that appears to have exposed the private and personal information of the agency's entire workforce."This is really bad for our undercover agents," says one former FBI agent, who fears for the safety of his colleagues.The former cyber investigator is in a group chat with current agents who are worried their personal information could soon be freely available online to criminals and hostile nation-state hackers.He says staff fear they could be targeted, or that criminals could use the data to create highly convincing phishing attempts, scams or demands for bribes.The hacking group ShinyHunters is threatening to publish the stolen databases and documents within four days unless its demands are met.Some agents are also concerned about the risk of physical attacks from cyber criminals they have investigated."One of the things we are discussing in the group chat is 'violence-as-a-service' attacks from young online gangs," says the former worker."They could use this information to harass an FBI agent who has worked on their cases."Groups similar to ShinyHunters - believed to be an English-speaking gang - have in the past been linked to swatting incidents, and even petrol bomb attacks against law enforcement officers and rivals.The group claims it breached FBI systems on Monday and later posted details of the attack on its darknet site.The FBI has not responded to requests for comment. However, on Wednesday the agency acknowledged the breach - saying it was "aggressively investigating" how it occurred.For Michael McPherson, a former FBI agent who is now senior vice president of security operations at cyber firm ReliaQuest, the hack presents "a security threat which cuts to the core of agent safety, particularly their families".He says agents understand the "inherent risks" that come with the job.

articles.title: Black woman found hanging from tree was dead before body was 'staged', police say
articles.excerpt: Warning: This story contains distressing detailsPolice in the US state of Mississippi have said that they believe a black woman was already dead before her body was "staged" and placed hanging in a tree.The disclosure was made in court by a detective on Friday, who also said they believed Tasia Fortune, a mother of four, had been killed in a dispute related to drugs.The 29-year-old's body was found hanging from a tree at an abandoned home in Jackson in August.The discovery sparked widespread fears in the majority-black city, due to the state's deep history of racial violence and lynchings. After weeks of speculation and demands for information, police made multiple arrests. In a news release, police said that the medical examiner had determined that Fortune's death was a homicide and that "the scene and the hanging were staged".Officials have not stated the exact cause of death or shared why they believe the hanging was staged.Fortune's mother told the BBC that she remembers the coroner telling her: "we're not treating this as [an] actual hanging." Her daughter, they told her, was dead before being placed in the tree. Spivey also recalled police telling her the incident was "drug related".Speaking to reporters outside the Jackson Police Department on Friday, Spivey described how she knows her daughter fought for her life till the very end."I know she did. I know my daughter," Spivey told reporters. Fortune leaves behind four young children, ages 7, 5, 4 and 1, she added.Dressed in a shirt that reads "Justice for Tasia Fortune", Spivey stressed that she does not want to see any innocent people going to jail."I just hope they have the right people," she said.Three people have so far been arrested in relation to the case, all of whom are black, including Jarques Ratliff, 51, who has pleaded not guilty.

articles.title: Pope warns against 'losing humanity' to AI machines
articles.excerpt: Pope Leo XIV has issued a warning about the dangers of artificial intelligence (AI) at the start of his four-day visit to France.The pontiff cautioned against "losing our humanity amid a paradise of machines" in wide-ranging remarks to Church and state officials at the Élysée Palace, following an hour of talks with President Emmanuel Macron.Leo made a similar warning earlier this year when he spoke of the need for AI to be "disarmed" in the first major teaching document of his papacy.In his May appeal, he mentioned the slave trade in relation to AI, suggesting that the world was in danger of normalising the exploitation of people once again.The highpoint of Leo's visit to France is set to be a giant Mass attended by more than half a million people in Paris on Saturday, for which an altar has been built on the Place de la Concorde and a large area around the Champs-Élysées sealed off by police.Large crowds are expected throughout the trip, reflecting an enthusiasm that the Church attributes to growing spirituality among the French and other Europeans.He was greeted at Orly airport early on Friday by Macron, with the pair expected to deliver a speech later in the day in Metz.Crowds were meanwhile gathering along a route to the Notre Dame, where the pontiff will later be driven in his popemobile.The president will not be at any of the Pope's Masses, largely to avoid breaching France's strict separation of state and religion.On Friday, Macron hailed Pope Leo's visit to France as a "great honour", stressing that French secularism "in no way negates religion".Leo said that "authentic secularity" should not exclude religion "from the public sphere or from education".In recent years, French politicians have often invoked France's brand of secularism to justify bans on religious symbols, including Muslim women's attire, in public spaces and schools.The Champs-Élysées Mass will be attended by Macron's wife Brigitte and Prime Minister Sébastien Lecornu.

articles.title: Two arrested after people seen mysteriously emerging from various New York City sewers
articles.excerpt: New York officials arrested two of three men who they said were seen emerging from a manhole, exiting the city's underground sewer system on Wednesday. The New York Police Department (NYPD) arrested 26-year-old Kevin Rodriguez and 25-year-old Samuel Reveron on charges of conspiracy and trespassing. Three men were seen exiting a manhole near the hotel where Israeli Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu was reportedly expected to stay for the United Nations General Assembly. In a statement to the BBC, the NYPD said it had seen a number of incidents involving people going into the sewer system to look for valuables and scrap metal after a storm."This incident fits that same criteria, but out of an abundance of caution given the U.N. General Assembly and the sensitivity of the location, the NYPD is conducting additional security sweeps with our federal partners," the police department said in a statement. Rodriguez and Reveron, both from Queens, were arrested on Thursday. They allegedly fled the scene after climbing out of the manhole when officers were called around 4:30 EST (9:30 BST) on Wednesday, police said. During a hearing on Friday morning, the two men pleaded not guilty and were released from custody, according to court records. The arrests follow a string of incidents in which people were seen emerging from pavement manholes in different parts of the city in recent months. In August, surveillance footage showed a person coming out of a manhole in Queens early in the morning. The same month, the NYPD said it was investigating three people wearing overalls and headlamps seen climbing out of a manhole near Penn Station.In May, a group of people were captured on surveillance footage shifting a manhole cover and climbing down into the sewer in South Brooklyn.

articles.title: Supreme Court allows Trump to use controversial database to check voter citizenship
articles.excerpt: The US Supreme Court has lifted restrictions on the Trump administration to use a controversial federal database that uses citizenship information and other sensitive data to identify voters suspected of being non-citizens.Critics have questioned the reliability of the data, warning it could result in US citizens being wrongly removed from electoral rolls. In June, a federal judge ruled that the system was illegal and violated the privacy rights of Americans.But the top court's conservative majority ruled that the National Voter Registration Act prohibits broad purges of voter rolls in the weeks before an election, which limits any "potential impact" of the decision ahead of the midterms.But states can still check the citizenship of individual voters.The three liberal-leaning justices on the Supreme Court dissented from the majority decision.One of the dissenting Supreme Court justices, Ketanji Brown Jackson, expressed concern that this could mistakenly revoke the voting rights of eligible voters."The harm caused by burdening or disenfranchising even a few lawful voters outweighs the non-existent harm that the government experiences when it is prevented from taking an action that it likely lacks the authority to take," she wrote.The Department of Homeland Security programme, known as Systematic Alien Verification for Entitlements (Save), allows officials to verify the eligibility of voters on their rolls.The database was first created in 1986 to help officials verify the citizenship or immigration status of those applying for public benefits.

articles.title: Trump's plans for massive arch move ahead
articles.excerpt: Earlier this week Trump announced that the proposed "Triumphal Arch" would double as a complex to store military equipment, complete with the ability to deploy snipers and drones from the roof and plaza.In a letter to the Pentagon and Federal Aviation Administration (FAA), Duckworth said they "must reject this foolhardy plan and instead focus on increasing the safety of the airspace".The arch is to be built just outside Arlington National Cemetery in Virginia, and about 4mi (6km) from Ronald Reagan Washington National Airport, the site of the deadly 2025 midair crash between a military helicopter and commercial plane. "The American people cannot afford to stand witness to Trump's risky plan to place a 250-foot (72m) structure along a busy approach path, especially if he follows through on plans to station snipers on the arch and fly drones," Duckworth wrote in the letter, which was obtained by the BBC's US partner, CBS News. The FAA, however, ruled last week that the massive structure would not pose a risk to flights coming into and out of the airport. On Thursday, the Advisory Council on Historic Preservation, led by Trump appointees, announced it was ending required consultations with local officials about how the structure might affect 42 historic properties in the area.The council said in the announcement that the National Park Service, which oversees federal landmarks, had proposed a plan for mitigating potential harms to those properties, but local historic preservation officers "raised concerns with the purpose and need of the Triumphal Arch". They also questioned whether the service had adequately identified possible harms and planned sufficient actions to address them.Federal and state officials are not required to reach an agreement on a project's harm-mitigation plans, and those consultations are allowed to be terminated if both sides can't agree.

articles.title: Students strike across Germany in protest against military service
articles.excerpt: School strikes are taking place across Germany to protest against the possible reintroduction of compulsory military service.One of the organisers of the strike, Bela Breitner, from School Strike Against Compulsory Military Service said the federal government was "serious about gradually reintroducing compulsory military service".At one protest in Hamburg, demonstrators waved flags and held up banners emblazoned with the words "We won't take part in your wars".German Chancellor Friedrich Merz has made boosting Germany's military a priority following Russia's invasion of Ukraine.A new law introducing voluntary military service came into force in January, with the aim of recruiting volunteers to increase the number of soldiers.However, if the security situation worsens or if too few volunteers come forward, a form of compulsory military service could be considered by Germany's Parliament, the Bundestag.Under the law, all 18-year-olds in Germany are being sent a questionnaire asking if they are interested and willing to join the armed forces.One protester, 16-year-old Elias Bernhard, from Hamburg, said that the responses to the questionnaires "show that young people do not want to join the Bundeswehr [Germany's armed forces]"."That is why I am out on the streets today. That is why we are serious about striking until compulsory military service is off the table. We will carry on."The questionnaire is mandatory for men and voluntary for women.

articles.title: Man shot during 2024 Trump campaign rally in Butler dies
articles.excerpt: In a post on his social media site Truth Social, Trump called Copenhaver a "true American patriot". "More than two years ago in Butler, Pennsylvania, a crazed gunman attempted to stifle our America First Movement. Instead, Jim and so many other wonderful Patriots who love our Country, stood united in defense of our shared values of Freedom, Liberty, and Justice," Trump said. "Our hearts and prayers are with the Copenhaver family, especially his incredible wife Marianne."An attorney for Copenhaver's family said his dedication to the US was a "defining part of his life". "As a veteran, he proudly served our nation in the armed forces, and his love of country never wavered," the lawyer said in a statement to the BBC's US partner CBS News. In an interview with CBS a year after the Butler rally, Copenhaver and David Dutch, the third attendee who was shot, said they had been through infections and surgeries after being wounded. Copenhaver was shot in the arm and the abdomen. A year later, the bullet was still lodged in his body next to his spine, he told CBS, causing him to walk with a cane. Both Dutch and Copenhaver sued the federal government for damages in June, arguing the Secret Service failed to ensure their safety and was therefore liable for their injuries. Republicans in the US House of Representatives also paid tribute to Copenhaver on Friday, saying in a social media post: "Jim endured unimaginable hardship with strength and perseverance."

articles.title: Xi got Trump's red carpet welcome - but not everything he wanted
articles.excerpt: Figure caption, Watch: The world’s two most powerful men just met. How did it go?ByLaura BickerChina correspondentPresident Xi Jinping's summits with Donald Trump have one clear aim.China believes the United States is trying to contain its rise as a superpower, and it wants Washington to stay out of its way - particularly when it comes to trade, technology and Taiwan.On this visit, however, despite Trump rolling out the red carpet for him, the Chinese leader didn't get everything he wanted.The trade truce that saw both countries pause a tit-for-tat tariff war and prevent a further escalation, was extended by only a few months - from November to January.Beijing had hoped for at least a year as Xi looks to ride out the remainder of Trump's presidency.This means key disputes on tariffs, China's dominance on rare earth supplies and access to advanced US chips are being kicked forward into yet another round of negotiations.This suggests the US wants China to do more to fulfil its side of the bargain before offering longer-term concessions.Image source, ReutersImage caption, Trump and Xi attend a dinner at the White HouseThe uncomfortable truth for Xi is that his domestic economy is in trouble. While the country sells a record number of goods around the world, consumers at home are holding back. Youth unemployment remains stubbornly high and property prices have slumped in a country where 80% of people own their own homes.Trade is helping to prop up growth, making access to overseas markets more important than ever.

articles.title: Senior Kazakh officials detained after 14 service members swept out to sea
articles.excerpt: Five senior military officials have been detained in Kazakhstan following the death of 14 service members who were taking part in military exercises.Those who died were among a total of 17 who were swept into the Caspian Sea as they were disembarking from a boat on Thursday. Officials say the incident occurred "during a combat training mission due to a sharp deterioration in meteorological conditions and increasing winds".Three were rescued.Those detained include the chief of staff and first deputy commander of Kazakhstan's Naval Forces, two military unit commanders, and the commanders of a marine company and a boat. They are suspected of criminal negligence. An interior ministry committee has been set up to investigate the incident, which occurred some 43km (27 miles) from the city of Aktau in south-western Kazakstan.Deputy Interior Minister Sanzhar Adilov said a pretrial investigation into the deaths was being conducted.The investigation was looking into the decisions made during the organisation and execution of the military training exercise, whether safety requirements had been observed, and weather conditions had been taken into account - in addition to technical specifications of the boat.More than 500 military personnel, warships and coastal units were participating in the Caspian Defense 2026 military exercise, according to the Kazakh ministry of defence.

articles.title: Jay-Z rape accuser says her allegation was false
articles.excerpt: A woman who accused Jay-Z of raping her when she was 13 has formally said her allegation was untrue.The unnamed woman filed a lawsuit in 2024 claiming she had been drugged and raped by Jay-Z, real name Shawn Carter, and Sean "Diddy" Combs at a party after the MTV Video Music Awards in 2000.The stars denied the allegation and she dropped the lawsuit last year. Carter then sued her and her lawyers.In a statement filed in that case on Thursday, she wrote: "Shawn 'Jay-Z' Carter never raped me. I have never met or spoken to Mr. Carter. Mr. Carter never engaged in any inappropriate conduct toward me whatsoever."The woman, known in court documents by the pseudonym Jane Doe, also said: "My claims that Mr Carter and Mr Combs raped me while a third celebrity, [name redacted] watched are false. There is no truth to any of my claims against Mr Carter."I understand my false accusations have caused Mr Carter immense pain, suffering, and damage that can never be fully undone."Carter had vehemently denied the accusations, saying they were a "blackmail attempt" and describing them as "frivolous, fictitious and appalling allegations".When the accuser dropped her case in February 2025, the rapper, who is married to singer Beyoncé, said: "The trauma that my wife, my children, loved ones and I have endured can never be dismissed."The woman, from Alabama, has now been removed from Carter's lawsuit. She said she had not received any money from the rap superstar or anyone acting on his behalf, and had not been paid to make her latest declaration.The rapper is still suing the woman's former lawyers, led by Tony Buzbee.In a statement to Rolling Stone, external, which first reported Jane Doe's new declaration, Buzbee said he had not seen it.He said: "We have multiple lawyers (at least four) who dealt with Ms Doe long before she met me. She gave the exact same story to each.

articles.title: Internet restricted after fighting breaks out in Ethiopia's Tigray region
articles.excerpt: Internet and call services have been disrupted in Ethiopia's northern region of Tigray following the outbreak of fighting this week between regional forces and the national army.Services provided by state-owned telecoms operator Ethio Telecom have been completely cut, although those from the smaller private firm Safaricom remain operational. Internet monitoring group NetBlocks earlier posted on X that network data indicated a sub-national internet shutdown in northern Tigray."Last night telecommunications got knocked out," Duke Burbridge, an American humanitarian worker in Tigray's capital, Mekelle, told the BBC's Newsday programme.The BBC has contacted Ethiopia's authorities for comment.Sources have told the Reuters news agency that the group which controls Tigray, the Tigray People's Liberation Front (TPLF), ordered the communications blackout, with one suggesting it was to disrupt government drones.The TPLF has not commented.The BBC is unable to report from Tigray and surrounding areas.Even before the current disruption, finding video and images to establish what is happening on the ground has been a challenge.So far, other than footage from Mekelle, most of what has been shared online has been from outside the region.Clashes between Tigrayan forces and their allies and Ethiopia's federal troops broke out on Wednesday, prompting fears of a return to a full scale civil war and reports of panic buying.A humanitarian source in the neighbouring region of Afar told the AFP news agency there was "heavy fighting overnight", including drone strikes, around the town of Abala in the mountains between Afar and Tigray, as "federal forces pushed the rebels from entering the town".There have also been reports of fighting near the town of Lalibela in the Amhara region, which is home to churches hewn out of rock, recognised as a UN World Heritage site.

articles.title: US backs Elon Musk's bid to overturn €120m EU fine against X
articles.excerpt: The US government is seeking to join Elon Musk's legal challenge to overturn a €120m (£105m) EU fine against X over its blue tick badges.In December 2025, the European Commission said the platform "deceives users" by allowing people to pay for a blue verified check mark, because it is not "meaningfully verifying" who is behind the account.But US Assistant Attorney General Brett A.

articles.title: Netanyahu defends Israeli military action as delegates walk out before UN speech
articles.excerpt: Israeli Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu has fiercely defended his country's military campaigns in Iran, Gaza and elsewhere in the Middle East in a speech to the UN General Assembly. After dozens of delegates walked out in protest as he took to the stage, Netanyahu vowed to continue fighting: "We're going to win. We have no other choice."In response to the walkout, he said: "If there are any other moral cowards who haven't left the hall, please do so now."The Israeli leader also rejected accusations that Israel is committing genocide in Gaza.Hours earlier, in a recorded message Palestinian President Mahmoud Abbas told the UN that Israeli policies - in particular the illegal expansion of Jewish settlements in the occupied West Bank - threatened "the very life and existence of the Palestinian people on their homeland".He also said it jeopardised the two-state solution, which is an internationally backed formula for peace between Israel and the Palestinians.Abbas said that Palestinians were being subjected to "killing, destruction, starvation and attempts at displacement, as well as a genocidal war" in Gaza by the Israeli military.The Palestinian leader was addressing the annual gathering via a video link because he had been denied a US entry visa.Netanyahu, who is subject to an International Criminal Court arrest warrant for alleged war crimes, launched scathing attacks on nations and leaders who have criticised him."They accuse Israel, tiny Israel, of colonialism - some colonialism. And who's accusing us? Among them are people in Britain and in France.

articles.title: Africa's richest man helps fund $660m fuel pipeline between Ethiopia and Djibouti
articles.excerpt: Nigerian billionaire Aliko Dangote has announced that he is helping to fund a new $660m (£500m) fuel pipeline between Ethiopia and DjiboutiThe project will include a 120km- (75 mile-) pipeline connecting Djibouti's Damerjog port to a distribution facility in Dewele, Ethiopia, as well as storage capacity of about 400 million litres.It is expected to begin operations within 18 months.Ethiopian Prime Minister Abiy Ahmed said the pipeline would reduce the time needed to transport fuel from Djibouti's port to the Ethiopian capital, Addis Ababa, from five days to one.The first phase will transport key petroleum products, including jet fuel, diesel and petrol.Speaking at the ground-breaking ceremony, Dangote, Africa's richest man, said the project would strengthen Ethiopia's energy security and make its fuel supply chain more resilient.Landlocked Ethiopia relies heavily on Djibouti's port for imports, including petroleum products. The new infrastructure is expected to reduce pressure on existing transport systems supporting industries, including transport, aviation, agriculture and construction.Djibouti is also expected to benefit from increased port activity, job creation and higher government revenues.The project is part of Dangote's wider expansion of infrastructure and manufacturing businesses across Africa.Dangote Cement has production capacity of about 55 million tonnes a year, while his oil refinery in Nigeria currently has capacity to process 700,000 barrels of crude a day and is seeking to double that to 1.4 million barrels a day.The refinery recently listed 4.1 billion ordinary shares on the Nigerian stock exchange, aiming to raise about $1.63bn (£1.2bn).In Kenya, the company is due to break ground next week on a proposed 700,000-barrel-a-day crude oil refinery in Lamu.

articles.title: Italy ministers agree to ban burqa and niqab in school and cap foreigners in class
articles.excerpt: The Italian government has approved a ban on the burqa and niqab in schools, along with a limit on the share of pupils who speak little Italian in any one class. A 30% cap will be imposed on children without Italian citizenship or poor knowledge of the Italian language in the first year of primary, middle and high school.Prime Minister Giorgia Meloni described the measures as "common-sense tools that do not divide but really help to integrate".Opposition parties accuse the government of pandering to the policies of the hard-right Futuro Nazionale party, ahead of a general election next year.Education Minister Giuseppe Valditara has said the limit is "purely linguistic" rather than one of citizenship, while he has sought to frame the ban on the niqab and burqa as a matter of gender equality."You must go to school with your face uncovered," Meloni said while announcing the plans on Sunday, adding that no-one could decide that a young woman should hide herself in the name of tradition.There were several drafts of the decree ahead of Thursday's council of ministers meeting, however the core details were clear.The veil ban would apply to the burqa and niqab, but not the hijab, which leaves the face visible. The niqab is a veil for the face that leaves the area around the eyes clear. However, it may be worn with a separate eye veil. It is worn with an accompanying headscarf.The burka is a one-piece veil that covers the face and body. Often there is a mesh screen around the eyes to see through.Non-Italian citizens make up 11.6% of pupils in Italy's schools, according to the research institution Fondazione ISMU.The 30% limit on pupils who speak limited Italian will cover separate stages of education differently.In primary schools, it would cover non-Italian citizens who have either not been born in Italy or who have not attended at least two years of nursery school.

articles.title: As Merz scrambles for support, Germany's identity crisis is laid bare
articles.excerpt: A set of bumper local elections has thrown Germany, and its government, off balance.Chancellor Friedrich Merz may now be a man on borrowed time. His coalition government is in crisis.But this breakdown of business as usual in Germany has been brewing for years.It's a nation wrestling with new, uncomfortable and unresolved realities.Think of certain stereotypes about Germany, and think again.A country dominated by boring, consensus-driven politics? Not any more.A confident, powerhouse economy at the cutting edge of car-making? Yesterday's story.A nation that can be used as a byword for impressive efficiency?

articles.title: The treasured 'eternal snow' on this tropical island is about to disappear forever
articles.excerpt: The treasured 'eternal snow' on this tropical island is about to disappear foreverImage source, Project Pressure/Klaus TymannImage caption, Only small patches of snow remain on Papua's Sudirman RangeByAbraham UtamaBBC IndonesiaThe mountains of Papua are not far from the equator, but they've been topped with "eternal snow" for centuries.The peaks in this Indonesian region on the world's second-largest island, just north of Australia, have offered scientists countless insights into the Earth's climate history.They're also the epicentre of the spiritual universe for many Papuans - a Mecca or a Vatican, as one activist puts it.But now, nearly all the snow is gone.A century ago, the 300km (190-mile) stretch of the Sudirman Range had snow and permanent ice on all four of its major peaks.But now there are only small areas around Puncak Jaya, also known as Carstensz Pyramid, with any snow at all. These are expected to entirely disappear in a year or two.Glacier cover around the peak has shrunk from nearly 1,900 hectares (4,700 acres) in the 19th Century to about 16 hectares (40 acres) today. Almost entire glaciers have vanished within a human lifetime."There is a profound unfairness in this," says Marie Šabacká, a Czech glacier ecologist who travelled to Puncak Jaya last March in a bid to be among the last scientists to study Papua's "eternal snow".She says the tropical glaciers in Papua are unique because they are separated from other glacier systems by thousands of kilometres. Papua is home to the "last remaining tropical ice" between the Andes and Himalayas.Ice cores taken from the slopes of Puncak Jaya preserve a record of climate history.

articles.title: Are Ethiopians marching back to war in Tigray?
articles.excerpt: Are Ethiopians marching back to war in Tigray?Image source, ReutersImage caption, Tigrayan forces have been patrolling the streets of Tigray's capital, Mekelle, this weekByLucy Fleming and BBC AfricaFighting has erupted in Ethiopia's northern region of Tigray between regional forces and the national army.Tigray residents, who have been trying to recover from a brutal two-year war that ended in 2022, fear a return to full-scale conflict.There are reports of panic buying - and now internet and call services have been disrupted.This means people cannot get access to their money via digital apps in what has become a largely cashless society after ATMs stopped working several months ago.Why has fighting broken out now?It follows more than six months of worsening relations between the government and the Tigray People's Liberation Front (TPLF), the party that runs Tigray.The African Union (AU) brokered a peace deal, known as the Pretoria Agreement, between the two sides, ending the war nearly four years ago - but several issues have remained unresolved that have inflamed tensions.This year, both sides have been trading blame while troops have mobilised amid pockets of fighting.This week, major clashes erupted in Tigray and quickly spread into the neighbouring Afar and Amhara regions.

articles.title: From Nagaland to a path to the Oscars: Indian film brings a rarely seen world to global cinema
articles.excerpt: There is something pleasingly improbable about Angh.The film comes from Nagaland, a mountainous state of fewer than two million people on India's northeastern frontier, and is in Konyak, a tribal language unfamiliar to most Indians, never mind audiences abroad. It was director Theja Rio's first feature and most of its cast faced a camera for the first time.And yet, at the Toronto International Film Festival this month, this quiet film won the Platform Prize, a major juried award.The award is intended to recognise films with a particularly distinctive directorial voice. The jury praised Rio's "refreshing perspective" and the film's portrait of a world rarely encountered on the international screen.The win also gives Angh an unusual route towards the 2027 Academy Awards. Under new rules, winners of designated prizes at six international festivals can qualify for consideration in the International Feature Film category without relying solely on their country's official submission.This does not make Angh an Oscar nominee. But it does place a Konyak-language film from one of India's smallest states inside a global conversation from which such stories have been almost entirely absent.Rio still sounds slightly startled by it. When we speak in Delhi, roughly 72 hours after the win, he has barely had a moment to breathe - Toronto, flights, interviews, more interviews."There were a lot of good films in the competition", he says, including films by far more seasoned directors. His producers were confident. "They thought we were going to win. I wasn't."He is also less solemn than Angh might suggest. Before cinema, he wanted to be a rapper - "a kid from Compton instead of a kid from Nagaland", as he puts it.

articles.title: Why Australia chose the world's biggest political stage to reveal OpenAI hack
articles.excerpt: It's entirely possible other governments have been the victim of rogue AI agents.Former Australian government cybersecurity adviser Alastair MacGibbon told the BBC he'd heard whispers that several others have been notified of similar recent breaches by OpenAI agents."Some have chosen to not be public – that's every government's choice on how it wants to handle these things," he said. "The [Australian] government chose a time to release this to gain maximum publicity which is their wont to do."Revealing a data breach can of course be a risky strategy for governments - it leaves them vulnerable to criticism that their security systems aren't up to scratch. But the fact that no sensitive information was leaked put Australia in a stronger position to use the incident."Nobody has died," says the University of Queensland's associate professor Michael Noetel, who studies AI risks. "This is another canary in the coal mine. This sort of loss-of-control incident, even though it's minor now, is what CEOs are worried about getting worse over time."Though Australia has made a name for itself by taking a stand against social media companies, taking up the AI mantle now is another way for Australia to rein in big tech, says Tama Leaver, professor of internet studies at Curtin University in Perth."It's impossible to say for sure, but it seems incredibly likely that this was very carefully planned."

articles.title: Trump and Xi come face-to-face as US and China battle to win the AI race
articles.excerpt: Figure caption, A red carpet and military flyover - How Trump welcomed XiByJoe TidyCyber correspondent and Osmond ChiaBusiness reporter"Whoever wins AI, WINS!"US President Donald Trump has been blunt about his AI ambitions, as well as about who he considers the US's main rival to be: China.His Chinese counterpart, Xi Jinping, has not said anything so forthright - but it seems he holds a similar view."China very much sees it as a race, they very much think China should be the leading force in AI - they see AI as a power maximiser," says Rebecca Arcesati, from the Mercator Institute for China Studies.You can look beyond the rhetoric for evidence of this: AI has been a cornerstone of China's technological ambitions for more than a decade, whether Xi emphasises it publicly or not.For Trump, beating China to AI supremacy outweighs any risks of the technology to humans - something he has described as "a hoax".China's foreign ministry warned that "narratives of threat" and confrontation hinder global AI governance, calling for cooperation to ensure it benefits all.It means when the two presidents sit down on Thursday there will be few more important topics than their AI ambitions - and what they say and decide will matter to the whole world.Image source, ReutersImage caption, The US and China are locked in a race to develop AIIs the US in the lead?There's no doubt the US and China are global leaders in AI but who is ahead depends on how success is measured.American companies lead on so-called frontier models, with the highest-performing systems on most benchmarks coming from firms such as Anthropic, Google and OpenAI.In February 2025, an AI model by China's DeepSeek "briefly matched the top US model" and as of March 2026, Anthropic's top model led the pack "by just 2.7%", according to researchers at Stanford University, external.Part of the US advantage stems from the vast sums being invested in leading AI companies as the frontier labs burn through mountains of cash to

articles.title: In Amish country, nurses go door to door to stop deadly spread of measles
articles.excerpt: For the past few months, nurse Dale Weiser has been making unexpected home visits.As the state battles the deadliest measles outbreak in recent history, the clinical supervisor drives 30 miles (48.3km), sometimes daily, to a rural corner of Pennsylvania where many Amish people live.Walking into strangers' homes, Weiser says she tries her best to be respectful and non-intrusive as she vaccinates dozens of family members against the measles, sometimes around the kitchen table."A lot of people that I encounter, they don't have health insurance. They don't have a lot of interaction with the health system, and they just haven't seen the need to get these vaccines," said Weiser, who works for the Chester County Health Department."When you start talking and you answer their questions, and build that trust, a lot of times they will make a different decision."The at-home vaccinations are part of the county and state health departments' strategy to encourage immunisations in the county, which includes an Amish community who abstain from many aspects of modern life, including regular contact with the western medical system.Amish people began coming to the US in the early 1700s, with the first community settling in Lancaster, Pennsylvania. Known as the "Plain People" for the simple clothes they wear, the Amish are a devout Christian community that does not use many forms of technology, relying on horse and buggies instead of cars.About 90,000 Amish people live in Pennsylvania, with estimates suggesting around only a quarter of Amish people in the Lancaster area have had the MMR vaccine.There is no particular religious text advising against vaccines, but Amish people do not have regular contact with the western medical system, or have a way to easily travel to appointments, experts said."A lot of people who haven't gotten vaccinated, it's not because they have a strong stance against getting vaccinated for measles. It's just that they haven't gotten around to it.

articles.title: Thousands turn out to greet Pope in France
articles.excerpt: Pope Leo XIV has arrived in France for his four-day visit, where he has delivered an address ahead of a giant Mass to be attended by more than half a million people in central Paris. President Emmanuel Macron greeted the Pope at Orly airport, before he spoke at the Élysée Palace on geopolitical issues and artificial intelligence (AI).The BBC's Paris correpondent Hugh Schofield looks at why the visit is met with enthusiasm the Church attributes to growing spirituality among the French.

articles.title: Robbie Williams' surprise singalong after Peru gig cancelled
articles.excerpt: Robbie Williams gave an impromptu performance outside a hotel in Peru's capital Lima, after his concert at a stadium in the city was cancelled.Authorities announced that the Arena 1 Park gig could not go ahead, citing failures by the venue to comply with safety regulations.Robbie told fans outside his hotel he was "broken-hearted" and held a brief singalong with the cheering crowds.

articles.title: Pomp and toasts: Day 2 of Trump and Xi in DC
articles.excerpt: US President Donald Trump held talks with President Xi Jinping at the White House on the second day of the Chinese leader's visit to Washington DC. There was pomp and ceremony, but little in the way of confirmed progress on key issues. The day ended with a state dinner, which was attended by major tech CEOs including Tesla's Elon Musk and OpenAI's Sam Altman.Read more on this story here.

articles.title: Rebel offensive against Ethiopian army stokes fears of return to civil war
articles.excerpt: There are growing fears of a return to civil war in Ethiopia after an offensive by fighters from Tigray into the neighbouring states of Afar and Amhara and the formation of a new rebel alliance aimed at overthrowing the government of the prime minister, Abiy Ahmed.About 600,000 people died between 2020 and 2022 during a devastating war between the Ethiopian army and the political party and paramilitary group the Tigray People’s Liberation Front (TPLF). Both sides are now accusing the other of triggering a return to open conflict.On Sunday, seven armed groups from around the country, including the TPLF, announced the formation of the Ethiopian Peoples’ Forces Alliance for Survival, aimed at deposing the government in Addis Ababa. Then, on Wednesday, the TPLF seized control of three airports from federal police. The state-owned carrier, Ethiopian Airlines, said it had suspended flights to the region “due to the current situation”.The TPLF also launched attacks into Afar and Amhara. A humanitarian source in Afar told Agence France-Presse there were heavy artillery attacks by the group on Thursday as they attempted to take control of the town of Yallo, near the Tigrayan border.Flights to the historic Ethiopian town of Lalibela were also suspended on Thursday because of nearby fighting, while people in Tigray stocked up ⁠on food and cash, with one resident telling Reuters that people there feared they could face siege conditions similar to those during the previous war.A resident of Adigrat, a city close to the Eritrean border, ‌described panic-buying and shops emptying. “Food shortages are worsening as market shelves sit empty … Essential medicines remain scarce and astronomically expensive,” he told Reuters.

articles.title: Indian billionaire’s payments firm plots biggest London flotation in years
articles.excerpt: A payments business that operates across Africa and is ultimately controlled by an Indian billionaire has announced its intention to float on the struggling London Stock Exchange.Airtel Money, the mobile money arm of Airtel Africa, is planning one of the biggest UK listings in years, in a boost for the shrinking London market that has faced a string of recent departures.The company is understood to be hoping to raise about $800m (£601m) from the initial public offering (IPO) and is targeting a valuation of $8bn to $9bn, which would make it one of London’s largest listings in recent years.Airtel Money has 53 million monthly active users across 13 countries in sub-Saharan Africa, including Uganda, Zambia and the Democratic Republic of Congo.Sunil Bharti Mittal controls Bharti Enterprises. Photograph: Ludovic Marin/AFP/Getty ImagesIt operates through a network of branches and kiosks, which enable customers to load money on to their phones, withdraw cash and access other money services, and the company generated revenues of just under $1.4bn in the last financial year.Airtel Money’s parent company is Airtel Africa, a telecoms provider that is part of the Indian conglomerate Bharti Enterprises, which is ultimately controlled by the billionaire Sunil Bharti Mittal. Airtel Africa is already listed on the FTSE 100 but said it wanted Airtel Money to be listed separately.“From a company perspective, [the listing] gives us flexibility for the future,” said Airtel Money’s chief executive, Ian Ferrao.“We evaluated multiple [stock] exchanges, including the Middle East because we’ve got a headquarters in Dubai, along with European and North American exchanges. Ultimately, shareholders felt that London was the right choice.

articles.title: Top South African police officer charged with raping woman, 18, and grooming 16-year-old girl
articles.excerpt: One of South Africa’s most senior police officers has been charged with raping an 18-year-old woman and grooming a 16-year-old girl, as the country’s police face allegations of corruption and failing to tackle violence against women and girls.Shadrack Sibiya, who was already suspended from his role as deputy national police commissioner over allegations he interfered with political killings investigations, was arrested on Monday. He is facing charges of rape, people trafficking, promoting the sexual grooming of a child and two counts of grooming a child.Sibiya appeared briefly in a Johannesburg court on Tuesday. He was then taken to prison in the capital, Pretoria, before a bail hearing on 29 September, as prosecutors had argued he was an escape risk.South Africa is reeling after the discovery of nine women’s bodies across Ekurhuleni, the municipality east of Johannesburg, in September. Meanwhile, the Madlanga Commission judicial inquiry has been examining allegations of corruption and criminality within the police for the last year.Puleng Dimpane, the acting national police commissioner, said: “Police officers are entrusted with protecting women and children. They cannot themselves be implicated in conduct that undermines this responsibility. As the country continues to confront the scourge of gender-based violence and femicide, there can be no room for anyone within the police service who is alleged to abuse their position or violate the rights of women and children.”Sibiya is accused of raping an 18-year-old woman at a hotel in May in the Sandton business district of Johannesburg. The alleged rape took place “whilst she was passed out due to intoxication administered by the accused”, according to a copy of the charge sheet.The alleged grooming of the 16-year-old girl took place over WhatsApp between 20 July and 3 August, according to the charge sheet.

articles.title: Healthcare in Africa ‘under growing strain’ after US withdrawal from aid programs, report warns
articles.excerpt: The United States’ withdrawal from key aid programs has put healthcare in Africa and the global south “under growing strain” a new report warns.The report says the Trump administration’s cuts to programs such as US Agency for International Development (USAID), as well as the Covid-19 pandemic and rising costs of living globally have brought “new urgency” for the need to reform healthcare in the region.The report, titled A Sovereign Future For Health, was created by the Accra Reset, a global health initiative led by John Dramani Mahama, Ghana’s president, that believes countries in Africa and the wider global south should have greater control over their health development rather than being dependent on aid from western countries and international institutions.A key statistic cited by Mahama and Accra Reset is that Africa produces less than 1% of its vaccines while carrying about 25% of the global disease burden.The report cites how abrupt changes to global health financing, such as the US withdrawal from several global health initiatives, forced countries within the global south to urgently restructure their finances. The report points to the Trump administration’s decision to dissolve USAID, which pushed Nigeria to absorb the 28,000 health workers who were previously employed by the agency at a cost of $200m.External financing for health in Africa contracted by close to 70% between 2021 and 2025, the report notes, meaning that African countries historically dependent on aid were forced to adapt quickly.The withdrawal of the US Emergency Plan for Aids Relief (Pepfar) funding for South Africa, which provided over $400m a year annually and is credited with saving 26m lives globally since 2003, led to HIV clinics closing across the country.

articles.title: Banished to alien lands: Trump’s secret deportation deals
articles.excerpt: Nika’s storyNo one would tell the shackled detainees onboard the US immigration plane where they were going. The officers in charge would taunt them when they asked, they said. It was only when the seat-back video screens finally showed a map that the 18 migrants worked it out.Their destination was Central African Republic (CAR), a country few of them had even heard of.Nika, a 32-year-old Iranian woman, recalled how the handcuffs dug into her wrists. She begged the officers to loosen them, but they did not. Other passengers had it worse, she said. Some of the men were restrained in black and yellow body wraps, as if mummified, after resisting orders to get on the plane.Nika, who had fled Iran 18 months earlier after protesting against its regime, had imagined the US as a place of sanctuary. Iran was already one of the most repressive countries in the world when she left, and its horrors had only deepened since then: security forces gunned down thousands of other demonstrators this year, then Donald Trump’s administration launched the war there.After more than a year locked up in a US immigration detention centre, Nika, whose name the Guardian has changed to protect her family in Iran, was granted legal protections and freed on a judge’s orders. Within two weeks, the Department of Homeland Security had rearrested her, and days later she was on the plane heading 7,000 miles east.“They never told me they were going to deport me [to] this country,” she told the Guardian. “I don’t know anything about Africa.”The Department of State warns US citizens not to travel to CAR because it says it is too dangerous. Nika spends most of her days there under a form of self-imprisonment, too scared to venture out from her small bedroom as she waits for an answer to the question on which her life depends: will she be sent back to Iran, and to a regime that could kill her?Nika is one of more than 25,000 people deported by the Trump administration to countries that are not their own.

articles.title: Michigan CEO loses job after posting AI-made image of her family in ‘Lake America’ sweaters
articles.excerpt: The CEO of a Michigan credit union is no longer employed there, according to the organization, after she posted on social media what appeared to be an AI-generated image of her and her family wearing sweaters emblazoned with the Donald Trump-associated words “Lake America”.In the statement recently announcing that Jane Smith would no longer be its CEO, Family First Credit Union also apologized “for the concern, disappointment and pain this situation has caused”.Smith had been the chief executive officer of the Family First Credit Union when she posed for a family photo at the Detroit airport en route to Halifax, Canada. She reportedly used ChatGPT to edit the family’s sweaters to say Lake America, which since late August has been the name that Trump ordered the US’s federal government agencies to use for Lake Ontario amid the president’s trade war with Canada.Smith then shared the image on Facebook on 11 September – the 25th anniversary of the 9/11 terrorist attacks in the US – along with the caption: “Like our sweatshirts? Not sure Canada will.”The post ended with “Lol lol”. It went viral and then provoked backlash from people in Canada – where a portion of the lake is.Those online users found it disrespectful, and the post has since been deleted according to Canadian Broadcasting Corporation (CBC) News.Many in the comments highlighted that the post was particularly insensitive, given Halifax’s role in hosting thousands of stranded airplane passengers who were diverted there when US airspace closed on the day of the 9/11 attacks.As the controversy intensified, Family First Credit Union – based in Saginaw, Michigan – said it was reviewing the situation. Smith, meanwhile, apologized, expressing regret, maintaining that the post was the result of poor judgment and saying that she understood why it would be offensive.“We weren’t trying to make a political statement,” Smith told the Detroit television news station WJRT.

articles.title: Alberta’s self-image as world’s only rat-free region shattered by discovery of rat
articles.excerpt: For more than seven decades, residents of Alberta have shared something in common with Antarctica and the high Arctic: all locations are officially free of rats.But on Thursday the Canadian province’s reputation as a firewall against rodent infestation took a hit when the town of Bowden announced the discovery of a dead rat and called on the province’s “rat patrol” to investigate.“If you’ve noticed rat droppings or any signs of rats, please contact Rat Patrol Alberta so they can follow up,” the town said in a statement. “Please stay alert and report any sightings.”Officials in Bowden did not say where in the town the rat was found.But as global temperatures increase, rat numbers have surged in major cities. Over the past decade, rats increased by 390% in Washington DC, 300% in San Francisco and 162% in New York, according to researchers, who analysed public sightings and infestation reports. Toronto, Canada’s largest city, is facing a “perfect rat storm”, with numbers up 186% in the last 10 years.Unlike other regions in the world that have been overrun by the wily and adaptable urban mammals, Alberta has actively fought rats from entering at all.“Albertans have enjoyed living without the menace of rats since 1950 when the Rat Control Program was established,” the province says in its rat guide.It cites both the province’s unique geography, with mountain ranges and boreal forest surrounding most of Alberta, and the fact that the Norway rat – “one of the most destructive creatures known to man”, the province claims – cannot survive in vast natural areas and cannot overwinter in cultivated fields.

articles.title: Hurricane Polo barrels towards Baja California region of Mexico
articles.excerpt: Hurricane Polo is barreling towards the Baja California region of Mexico, the latest system in a Pacific hurricane season that has been notably active in recent months. On 22 September, a measurement of 892 millibars was registered for Hurricane Polo, making it the second-most intense hurricane on record in the east Pacific. It is fuelled by exceptionally warm waters across the Pacific Ocean, providing favourable conditions for the system to maintain its considerable strength.Polo is expected to turn towards the west-north-west, before taking a more north-westerly trajectory on Saturday. It has maximum sustained winds of around 150mph, with even stronger gusts occurring within the most intense parts of the hurricane. Hurricane-force winds extend outward for approximately 40 miles from the centre, while tropical storm-force winds reach as far as 125 miles. These powerful winds, combined with torrential rainfall and dangerous seas, could have significant impacts. Although some fluctuations in intensity are possible over the coming days, Polo is expected to remain powerful as it tracks north-westwards.In India, a deep 988-millibar low-pressure system – a tropical storm in this case – is centred along the east coast, bringing widespread and potentially disruptive weather conditions to Odisha and surrounding areas. The system is producing heavy rainfall across the region, with the latest forecast models suggesting totals could exceed 200mm in some locations over a 24-hour period. Rainfall rates are expected to be particularly intense at times, with hourly totals potentially exceeding 30mm in the heaviest downpours. Such intense rainfall could cause significant surface water and localised flooding, particularly in low-lying areas and places with poor drainage. Strong and gusty winds are also affecting coastal parts of Odisha.

articles.title: Lula says Trump wants to ‘colonise’ and capture Brazil’s resources by meddling in election
articles.excerpt: Luiz Inácio Lula da Silva’s presidential campaign has accused Donald Trump of wanting to “colonise” Brazil in order to capture its natural resources by meddling in next month’s presidential election.The accusation came in a campaign advert that was published on social media on Thursday night by Lula’s team and will air on television on Friday amid growing fears over the impact alleged US interference could have on the vote.The TV spot claims the US president is trying to sway the election in favour of Lula’s far-right adversary in the election, Flávio Bolsonaro, in order to advance Trump’s interests in the South American nation.“Flávio Bolsonaro is Trump’s candidate and what Trump wants is to colonise Brazil, take our riches, steal our future and leave us in the dust,” the female narrator tells viewers in the minute-long video.The state department has denied claims the US is meddling in Brazil’s election. “Any insinuation of a ‘ploy’ to undermine a democratic nation’s election is a baseless lie,” it said last month in a statement.Writing on X, Lula accused Bolsonaro of wanting to “hand our natural resources over to the United States”.“If it’s up to him, Brazil will become a colony again,” the incumbent leftwing president added.With just over a week to go until the 4 October first round vote, Lula and Bolsonaro are neck and neck in the polls. A second round run-off will be held on 25 October if no candidate secures more than half of the votes.In recent weeks, there has been growing alarm – both in Brazil and overseas – about Washington’s apparent attempts to influence the result, with a campaign of diplomatic and economic pressure, including 25% tariffs on Brazilian imports.Workers prepare electronic voting machines during a sealing operation before being used in the first round of Brazilian elections.

articles.title: Democratic lawmakers accuse Trump administration of interference in Brazilian elections
articles.excerpt: A group of 31 Democratic members of the US Congress has sent a letter to the secretary of state, Marco Rubio, criticising the Trump administration over “an apparent effort to interfere with, and potentially undermine” Brazil’s elections.Latin America’s largest country will hold the first round of its presidential election on 4 October, with polls showing a technical tie between the incumbent leftist president, Luiz Inácio Lula da Silva, and the far-right senator Flávio Bolsonaro.In the letter sent to Rubio on Thursday, 30 members of the House of Representatives and the senator Bernie Sanders listed a series of measures the US government took that they interpret as attempts to secure a victory for Flávio Bolsonaro, the son of former president Jair Bolsonaro.They wrote that those actions “reflect a broader and deeply troubling pattern of interference by the Trump administration in recent electoral processes across Latin America”, citing the recent midterm elections in Argentina and presidential elections in Honduras and Colombia.In July, a group of 11 Democratic members of Congress sent a similar letter arguing that Trump was trying to interfere in Colombia’s election in favour of the far-right millionaire and former lawyer Abelardo de la Espriella, who went on to win the second round.In Thursday’s letter, the lawmakers wrote that US officials under Trump have engaged in a “sustained, multifaceted campaign of interference and destabilization in Brazil”.They noted that when Trump imposed his first tariffs on Brazil last year, he made clear that one reason was Bolsonaro’s trial over his attempt to stage a coup after losing the 2022 election to Lula.

articles.title: Pomp over progress in Xi’s US summit with Trump is a win for China
articles.excerpt: If the Beijing meeting between Donald Trump and Xi Jinping in May was the “stalemate summit”, the second round of talks between the presidents of the US and China this week seemed to give up entirely on the idea of breakthroughs.Instead, it was described as a celebration of “diplotainment” rather than diplomacy, where pomp prevailed over progress and where one of the main outcomes was the news that two giant pandas would soon be sent from China to Atlanta zoo.Trump rolled out the red carpet for Xi’s arrival on Wednesday and broke with decades of precedent to meet the Chinese leader at Joint Base Andrews. Thus began a three-day state visit that involved a tour of Trump’s new helipad and the Marine One helicopter, and a 90-minute meeting that Trump described as “great” and that revealed, according to Trump, that Xi “has great interest in granite”.“The biggest takeaway is that Trump has been displaying an extraordinary degree of deference to Xi Jinping,” said Julian Gewirtz, who served as a senior China official in the Biden administration.But what of actual substance? Expectations going into the summit were low. But the outcomes somehow still fell short.Expectations going into the summit were low. Photograph: Saul Loeb/AFP/Getty ImagesOne of the biggest issues in the US-China relationship is trade. Last year, as Trump unveiled successive rounds of tariffs on Chinese goods, the White House accused China of unfair practices that it said contributed to the loss of 3.7m US jobs and inflated the trade deficit. The tariffs were supposed to suppress the volume of Chinese imports to the US and put pressure on China.To some degree, they worked. The US trade deficit with China in 2025 fell to $200bn, down from nearly $300bn in 2024.

articles.title: At Trump meeting, Xi Jinping lays out terms to avoid US-China military conflict
articles.excerpt: Xi Jinping has called for extensive cooperation with Washington to avoid the “Thucydides trap” that could put the US and China on a military collision course amid rising tensions over artificial intelligence, trade and Taiwan.At the start of his summit meeting with Donald Trump in the White House, the Chinese president laid out terms for a mutual understanding that he said could steer the two competing superpowers away from future military conflict and on to a road of mutual gain.Rather than confrontation, conditions for “achieving the great rejuvenation of the Chinese nation and making America great again go hand in hand” and should be the goal, Xi said, citing Trump’s political catchphrase.“We should strengthen communication. China and the United States are different in national conditions, but through candid, in-depth and continued dialogue, our two countries can understand each other better, seek common ground while shelving differences, and build up mutual trust,” said Xi, with Trump looking on.“We should coexist in peace. China and the United States, as two major countries, stand to gain from cooperation and will both lose in confrontation. Our two militaries should maintain regular dialog and improve mechanisms for crisis communication and prevention.”With such conditions in place, Xi said, “the Thucydides trap can be overcome”, referring to the phenomenon, defined by the Greek historian, of tensions that arise when an emerging power challenges the dominance of an established power.Xi invoked the phrase in his meeting with Trump in Beijing in May, asking the US president how he planned to avoid it.His proposals for lessening tensions – which also included the invitation of 100,000 young Americans to visit China on student exchanges – come amid a period of intense competition between the two powers over artificial intelligence and trade, with each side imposing tariffs on the other.Trump and Xi speak next to Marine One at the White House.

articles.title: Trump swoons over strongman soulmate Xi – are you feeling jealous, Vladimir?
articles.excerpt: One is an authoritarian who represses the media and has a strong allergy to democratic elections. The other is head of the Chinese Communist party.Donald Trump welcomed the Chinese president, Xi Jinping, to the White House on Thursday, setting the stage for a scene quite unlike anything the august old building has seen over more than two centuries.“Remarkably,” observed the US president, “this is our first time meeting together here at the White House, and as President Xi has already seen, a lot has changed since he was last here.”While Xi remained poker-faced, only a brief look around a grand foyer bedecked with American and Chinese flags would have verified Trump’s statement. On one wall, where an official portrait of Barack Obama once hung, was the dramatic image of a bloodied Trump with fist raised urging his supporters to “fight!” after a failed assassination attempt.And while Chinese state media had been welcomed onto the White House grounds, many US journalists had not, thanks to Trump’s ban on CNN, MS Now and Politico. Michael McFaul, a former US diplomat, described the vivid contrast as “wrong and embarrassing”.That was hard to deny, given that China ranks 178th in Reporters Without Borders’ press freedom index, ahead of only North Korea and Eritrea (the US, for the record, is down to 64th). But it also made perfect sense because, whereas past presidents sought to make China more like the US, Trump evidently aspires to make the US more like China.Trump and Xi walk along the Colonnade at the White House. Photograph: Annabelle Gordon/Abaca/ShutterstockThe deference was deafening.

articles.title: Rick Wakeman performs piano concert to 150 rescued moon bears in Vietnam
articles.excerpt: Rick Wakeman has played to all kinds of people around the globe, but he has now performed to an audience he had never encountered before – an enclosure of 150 bears.The former Yes musician, who has gone on to have a prolific solo career, played the piano at a Vietnamese bear sanctuary.“Before you ask, I won’t be playing the teddy bear’s picnic,” he joked ahead of the performance. Wakeman, who is a supporter of animal welfare causes and has rescue dogs and cats of his own, is conducting the concert to raise awareness of moon bears kept in cruel conditions for the extraction of their bile.He said he was a bit worried about how hot it is going to be. “You know the heatwave we had in England? It’s double that,” he said. “They offered to rig up a fan for me, but I figured that will just blow more hot air around.”A moon bear at the bear sanctuary in Tam Dao national park, Vietnam. Photograph: Luong Thai Linh/EPAHis concert was performed live on a Yamaha grand piano positioned in Animals Asia’s bear sanctuary in the Tam Dao national park, and Wakeman had written some new compositions especially for rescued bears.Asked whether the bears would enjoy the music, he said: “They’ve not got much choice, really. It’s a well-known fact that all animals react to music, especially gentle melodic music. So what I am going to do is piano music that is melodic, and I can only hope that they will come up to the perimeter of the sanctuary and have a listen.”Rick Wakeman plays piano at bear sanctuaryWakeman has been sponsoring rescue bears since 2016 and recently adopted a new one: “He’s only 20 months old, a big fella, I went to see him today. He came out right to the edge and stood on his back legs and just stared at me, it was brilliant.”Bile is extracted from bears for traditional Chinese medicine by putting a needle into their gall bladder and drawing it out.

articles.title: Alarm bells sound in Brussels as EU sales of Chinese hybrid cars rocket
articles.excerpt: Sales of Chinese hybrid cars have rocketed in the EU in the past four and a half years, data shows, underlining growing concerns in Brussels over the future of the European car industry.In 2022, just 659 Chinese-made fully hybrid cars (vehicles in which the petrol or diesel engine charge the motor and battery) were sold in the EU. However, after Brussels imposed anti-subsidy tariffs on fully electric cars from China in 2024, sales of hybrids have shot up to 160,662 in the first seven months of this year.Eurostat figures show that sales of Chinese-made plug-in hybrid vehicles – models popular for longer driving distances that can recharge via both the fuel engine and an external power source – have also soared, rising from 56,706 sold in 2022 to 217,764 from January to July this year.The volume of Chinese hybrids on the roads is now spooking the car industry and Brussels, which has asked China to voluntarily reduce its hybrid exports to the EU or face safeguards, likely to be quotas.On Thursday the German car industry for the first time indicated it would be willing to consider tariffs on Chinese hybrids specifically.The German Association of the Automotive Industry, VDA, called on the European Commission to carry out a comprehensive assessment of the impact of any trade safeguards, which can range from quotas to price floors and tariffs.It said: “The EU must also have an effective and up-to-date set of trade defence instruments at its disposal.

articles.title: Free the Strip! Melburnians fight back against outlawing of much-loved picnic spot
articles.excerpt: It looked like a typical spring evening on Melbourne’s Canning Street when a few dozen picnickers gathered on the grassy median strip on Friday, with drinks in hand.People in one group who’d come with a full alfresco setting chattered as they ladled punch out of a glass bowl on a wooden table, set with a tablecloth and yellow flowers in a vase. Others sat on picnic blankets, passing around bags of chips.What set this gathering apart was that it was actually against the rules, given the new ban against drinking on the strip. And the picnic had been organised in protest, part of a political saga that is unfolding on one of inner Melbourne’s most beloved streets.Protesters on Melbourne’s Canning Street. The median strip, beloved as a social spot, has become a political talking point after drinking on the grass was banned. Photograph: Catie McLeodIt began on Monday, when a local bar and bottle shop, the Wine Corner Store, announced on Instagram that, “due to a few unrelenting miserable neighbours who have been non-stop complaining to the council”, consuming alcohol had been outlawed on the median strips on Drummond, Rathdowne and Canning Streets in Carlton North.Sign up for the Breaking News Australia emailThe council was reverting to a former classification of the median strips – which are much wider than a typical nature strip – with the effect that they are no longer treated as park spaces. The council said residents had complained about noise, rubbish and unsafe behaviour.The community fought back to keep a tradition that has endured for many years. While the council ban followed an initial 29-signature petition that a resident submitted in August, a counter petition calling on council to revoke the ban gathered more than 7,707 signatures in just a few days.The protest drinks on Friday were civilised.Amid the uproar – and with people loosely uniting under a banner of Free the Strip!

articles.title: OpenAI hack on Australian government reveals anxiety at heart of global artificial intelligence dilemma
articles.excerpt: When the Australian prime minister, Anthony Albanese, sat down for an interview in the heart of Silicon Valley at the weekend he had known for two days that his was the first government known to have been attacked by a rogue AI agent.He didn’t reveal the attack then, but he sounded a warning about the march of AI: “the risk is that AI develops in a way in which humans are no longer in control of what AI is producing.”But Albanese noted, too, that two countries – the US and China – would dominate the world’s response to the new technology.“The truth is they’re the big two giants here, and so we want to see cooperation,” Albanese said.“The US is essentially ahead of China when it comes to the race that is on for the development of this new technology.

articles.title: ‘Robust little’ vessel begins treacherous 22,000km journey around Antarctica in the name of climate science
articles.excerpt: A small uncrewed vessel has embarked on a lap around Antarctica and may not return for months.The seven-metre craft, which looks like a large kayak in hi-vis orange, is expected to travel about 22,000km through inhospitable waters, propelled by powerful westerly winds and energy from the sun. The journey is seven times the distance between Sydney and Perth.Along the way, it is expected to encounter massive waves, freezing temperatures, ferocious winds, and even the odd curious seal or albatross.The mission?
