To collect data on carbon dioxide in the ocean and atmosphere, to help scientists better understand the role of ocean sinks.Dr Elizabeth Shadwick, a principal research scientist at the CSIRO, said that after leaving Hobart the vessel would travel east towards New Zealand, “eventually scooching through the Drake Passage between the bottom of South America and Antarctica, then coming along past South Africa and back to us here, where we’ll pick it up.”She hoped to see it again in seven to nine months.The vessel has a heavy keel to keep it upright and a solar sail to power it. Photograph: CSIRO AAPPThe autonomous vehicle made by the US maritime company Saildrone was designed to withstand the intrepid voyage, with a heavy keel keeping it upright, a rudder to steer and a fixed solar sail poking above the surface. It would be remotely monitored by the company, who would check in regularly via satellite, and, if necessary, nudge it in the right direction.“It’s already been bashed around pretty heavily,” Shadwick said. “It’s quite a robust little device.

articles.title: NSW crackdown on ‘AI-doctored’ real estate listings hits mural-covered wall
articles.excerpt: The New South Wales government’s crackdown on “AI-doctored” rental listings has hit a wall, after it made an example of a supposedly manipulated ad that turned out to be a genuine photograph of a $5,000 courtyard mural of Bondi beach.In a media release on Friday announcing protections against misleading rental ads, the state government provided a link to a property in Leichhardt, claiming it was an “AI-doctored rental listing in Sydney’s inner west”.But the listing agency IB Property denied the images were altered.A spokesperson confirmed the photograph showed a mural of Bondi beach on an internal courtyard wall visible through the unit’s windows, rather than a false digital depiction of coastal views.“We can confirm that the image has not been altered or digitally generated using AI, Photoshop or any other image-editing software,” the spokesperson said.The apartment’s original view, when listed in August 2014. Photograph: realestate.com.auLeichhardt is about 12km away from Bondi beach.When Guardian Australia visited 2/14 Norton Street, the artwork was not visible from the street. IB Property explained the mural sits within an internal courtyard and provided photos taken inside the unit confirming it remains in place.“The mural was commissioned and paid for by the landlord at a cost of approximately $5,000, and we can also confirm that there are no plans for it to be removed,” the spokesperson said, adding that the property was leased in February 2026 and had not been advertised since.A photo from 2026 showing a different view from the kitchen windows.

articles.title: Pocock calls for AI safety act after Medicare breach – as it happened
articles.excerpt: From 21h agoDavid Pocock calls for AI safety act after agent breachThe independent senator David Pocock says the recent AI agent breach raises serious questions about Australia’s approach to artificial intelligence regulation.Speaking on the ABC’s Afternoon Briefing, Pocock said the incident demonstrated the need for the government to introduce an AI safety act. double quotation markThis is not a new problem. For many years now experts have been saying we need action on this. The crossbench has been pushing them. The government then said, ‘we’ll have some guardrails, we’ll put them on a website’ … that’s not enough. Clearly it’s not. This is a huge challenge facing us. Senator David Pocock. Photograph: Sarah Wilson/AAPKey events21h agoWhat we learned today, Friday 25 September21h agoDavid Pocock calls for AI safety act after agent breach22h agoRetrial date for UK rapper accused of raping Australian fan24h agoAlbanese said AI breach information was released as soon as possible1d agoAngus Taylor says Anthony Albanese is ‘swanning around New York’ for UN summit1d agoNSW renter rights strengthened in latest tranche of Minns reforms1d agoAlbanese pitches for Australia to join UN security council1d agoJane Hume says AI breach shows we need more AI in Australia1d agoAI government website hack a ‘wake-up call’, Albanese says1d agoPolice officer killed in crash in Sydney1d agoGen Z going without for a house1d agoOpposition defence spokesperson says PM’s AI hack timing not a coincidenceWhat we learned today, Friday 25 SeptemberThat’s a wrap on our live coverage for today!Before we go, let’s recap the day’s top headlines: Anthony Albanese has called the first reported artificial intelligence agent hack into an Australian government website a “wake-up call” of the dangers of the technology.

articles.title: British climber, 28, dies in fall in northern Spain
articles.excerpt: A British man has died after falling about 61 metres (200ft) while descending from the summit of a mountain in northern Spain, according to local law enforcement.The 28-year-old mountaineer fell down a vertical gully on the east side of the Torrecerredo – the highest peak of the Cantabrian mountains – on Thursday afternoon, the Spanish Civil Guard for the Asturias region said.The mountaineer’s remains were located after a rescue team aboard a helicopter flew over the area, the Civil Guard said.Two specialists were lowered to retrieve the man’s body and his belongings which had been scattered during the fall.The incident occurred during the descent, about 20 metres below the Torrecerredo peak, the Civil Guard said.The mountaineer’s body was transported to La Morgal, a regional sports and aviation facility in Llanera near the Asturian city of Gijon.A spokesperson for the UK Foreign Office said it had contacted local authorities about the death.Torrecerredo, which has an elevation of about 2,649 metres, is the highest peak of the Picos de Europa mountain range, which is part of the larger Cantabrian Mountains range.

articles.title: Novelist accused of using AI to write book removed from French prize list
articles.excerpt: The organisers of France’s most prestigious literary prize said they had removed a critically acclaimed novel by a Canadian-Haitian writer from the longlist after an anonymous online account claimed the book was “almost entirely” written by AI.The Académie Goncourt, a Paris-based literary organisation, said on Friday its decision to withdraw Thélyson Orélien’s novel C’était ça ou mourir (It Was That or Die) was “driven by the desire to preserve the integrity of the Goncourt prize and the academy itself, whose central role is to promote and honour literature written by women and men”.The Haiti-born author’s book is a lyrical first-person account of how a history and geography teacher flees a home country mired in gang violence and embarks on a perilous journey across 12 countries before finding a haven in Canada.Published in France by Grasset in August, it has sold about 35,000 copies and won the Prix du roman Fnac, with translation rights sold to more than 20 countries.The novel on display inside a bookstore in Paris. Photograph: Sarah Meyssonnier/ReutersAllegations that the book was written using AI emerged on X on 21 September, the same day It Was That or Die won the Fnac prize for best novel.An anonymous account called Balance ton Claude – a reference to Anthropic’s AI agent – said it had fed the novel into the AI detection software Pangram and found it to be “almost entirely” written by artificial intelligence.Questions have been raised over Pangram’s accuracy, and French media outlets have found other AI detection programmes that identified It Was That or Die as very probably written by a human.Orélien, 38, has denied the allegation, saying it was racially motivated. “I’ve always loved creating and writing,” he said. “I don’t see why I would use a machine.”He told the newspaper Libération that he used traditional language and rhythms that were Haitian and Caribbean.

articles.title: Pope Leo warns of AI threat to humanity at start of three-day France visit
articles.excerpt: Pope Leo has warned against losing humanity in a “paradise of machines” as he addressed global concerns over the dangers of artificial intelligence at the start of a three-day visit to France.“If we are to avoid losing our humanity amid a paradise of machines invading and conditioning our daily lives, there is an urgent need for people to be educated in ethical discernment, capable of seeing what is morally right,” he said in a speech at the Élysée.At a second address on Friday, the 71-year-old head of the Catholic church insisted that new technologies must “remain at the service of the human person rather than becoming yet another instrument of domination and injustice” in remarks to a gathering at the Paris headquarters ⁠of the UN culture and education body, ⁠Unesco.“Every science risks losing its proper meaning when pursued without ethics,” he said. “Certain artificial systems have even been given the name of our human faculty of thought: intelligence. At the same time, however, our ideas and relationships risk being impoverished by a process of dehumanisation.”He added: “While intelligence is attributed to computational systems, we struggle to recognise the inalienable dignity of human persons whose lives are judged according to the criterion of efficiency and when deemed no longer productive, rejected and discarded.”Leo also criticised world leaders who disrespect the ⁠rule of ⁠law, without naming individuals. “Instead of ​respecting ‌the law, ‌those in power invoke ‌it when it serves their interests and disregard it when it restrains them, treating even justice itself ‌as though it were a commodity to be ​bought and sold,” he said.Leo, who became pope in 2025, ⁠has been critical of the direction ​of ​global leadership in ​recent months. He ​said ‌the world was “being ​ravaged ​by a handful of tyrants” last April.Pope Leo with the French president, Emmanuel Macron, and his wife, Brigitte Macron, at the Élysée.

articles.title: Pope Leo warns against AI and says technology ‘must remain at service of humans’ during first visit to France – as it happened
articles.excerpt: From 13h agoTechnology 'must remain at service of humans,' and not become instrument of 'domination and injustice,' Pope Leo warnsIn his deliberations on what it means to be human, Pope Leo says “we are all born naked and in need; poor by birth, in need of bread, and words, and words of care and affection.”Only through becoming adult, “we risk forgetting it,” with people’s “humanity betrayed or cast aside, exploited or deceived.” “Life is no longer understood as a gift, but as a commodity. It is no longer viewed as a summons to care and responsibility, but as a product to be exploited.” He “to be human is to be free by nature,” and to “recognise [life’s] grandeur” and “immense potential.”But he says “to be human … implies a responsibility before history,” as “the human being is one who grows, learns, and works with both hands and mind.”He then talks about the tragedy of the second world war, when “humanity had come to realise that scientific progress, when severed from wisdom, can turn into a weapon of destruction.”He says 80 years later, the founding charter of Unesco – built on that recognition – still stands.Turning to the issue of technology, he says “our efforts in this domain must ensure that new technologies remain at the service of the human person, rather than becoming yet another instrument of domination and injustice.”In a strong passage, he warns: “Over the centuries, many tasks once performed by human beings have been entrusted to machines whose capabilities and applications have continued to expand. More recently, certain artificial systems have even been given the name of our human faculty of thought intelligence. At the same time, however, our ideas and relationships risk being impoverished by a process of dehumanisation. The paradox has become increasingly evident.

articles.title: Meloni accused of ‘running scared’ with cap on foreign children in classrooms
articles.excerpt: The Italian government has been accused of ramping up divisive rhetoric to try to court far-right voters ahead of next year’s general election after it passed a decree aimed at capping the number of newly arrived migrants in classrooms and banning the burqa and niqab in schools.The prime minister, Giorgia Meloni, who leads the far-right Brothers of Italy party, said her government had approved what she called “commonsense measures that do not divide but genuinely help to integrate”.Writing on social media, she said the measures included: “A limit of 30% in classrooms for students who do not adequately know Italian, plus tools to learn our language and a halt to burqas and niqabs in school.”The announcement was a toned-down version of comments she had made earlier in the week at an event organised by Brothers of Italy’s youth division. “It cannot be that in the classroom it is Italian children who feel left out because they’ve become the minority,” Meloni said as she vowed to “legally set the number of foreign students per class”.Thursday’s decree also sets out that in cases where students show persistent problems with integrating or struggling to learn the language, their parents will be referred to social services and will have to take free literacy and Italian language classes.

articles.title: Trump faces tough choices as Iran dangles deal to reopen Hormuz before US midterms
articles.excerpt: Iran’s seven-day timetable to reopen the strait of Hormuz and start talks on its nuclear programme has been pitched as a deal that could rapidly extricate Donald Trump from a political crisis but requires the US president to make difficult concessions.In the five days left before the proposed reopening of the strait, which is expected to relieve pressure on global energy markets, Trump would need to lift Iranian asset freezes, permit Iran to export its oil and, probably most difficult of all, order Benjamin Netanyahu to end Israel’s attacks on Hezbollah in Lebanon, thus achieving the “ceasefire on all fronts”.Iranian diplomats in New York said they thought a three-hour meeting earlier this week with the US envoy Steve Witkoff in which they laid out the seven-day plan was productive, but were doubtful the US would deliver.Iran nevertheless feels it has done the diplomatic spadework, taking the proposal to China for endorsement and ensuring that Oman, located on the south side of the strait, was also on board.The foreign minister, Abbas Araghchi, explained that the idea was to take the elements of the Iran-US memorandum of understanding that Trump signed in June and repackage and accelerate the process since, as they understood it, Trump had come to hate the MoU.“The conditions we have asked the US to meet is nothing new, nothing more than what was already in the Islamabad agreement, which was signed by the US president,” Araghchi said. But what is new is the speed.Iran’s foreign minister, Abbas Araghchi, says the new deal contains the elements of June’s memorandum of understanding.

articles.title: Saudi Arabia intercepts wave of Houthi missiles as oil climbs to one-week high
articles.excerpt: Saudi Arabia says it intercepted six ballistic missiles fired by Yemen’s Iran-backed Houthis, with the latest attacks pushing oil prices ⁠to a one-week high over fears of spiralling supply disruptions.The ⁠Saudi-led coalition in Yemen said the missiles were ⁠aimed at Taif in western Saudi ​Arabia and the Yanbu area on the Red Sea, with the Houthis claiming their attacks were aimed at “a sensitive target” in the capital Riyadh and on Saudi Aramco facilities in Yanbu.Oil prices climbed about 3%, but trade was volatile and prices came off session highs after reports the US and Iran discussed reopening the strait of Hormuz.The escalating attacks threaten Saudi Arabia’s ⁠ability to export oil through the Red Sea at a time when the strait of Hormuz is disrupted and the kingdom’s east-west pipeline is only now resuming operations after drone strikes earlier ​this month.

articles.title: Susan Sarandon and Hannah Einbinder arrested at anti-Netanyahu protest in New York
articles.excerpt: Oscar-winning actor Susan Sarandon and Hacks star Hannah Einbinder were among people detained by police in New York on Thursday as they moved in to break up a protest against Benjamin Netanyahu.Agence France-Presse footage shows NYPD officers cuffing Thelma & Louise star Sarandon at the demo in the city as the Israeli prime minister was readying to address the United Nations general assembly.The New York Post reported Einbinder had also been marched away from the demonstration organised by Jewish Voice for Peace, where protesters held banners that read “Stop Arming Israel” and “End the Genocide.”A spokesperson for the NYPD said officers had responded to reports of an “unscheduled demonstration” where people were blocking an intersection.Hannah Einbinder (R) with Saturday Night Live star Sarah Sherman (L) at the protest. Photograph: Eric Cox/Reuters“Members of the NYPD Community Affairs Bureau issued … warnings, advising participants that they should leave,” the spokesperson said.“They continued to block the intersection. Multiple individuals who didn’t comply were taken into custody,” she said, without providing the number of people arrested.Democratic congressional candidate Darializa Avila Chevalier and New York ⁠City council member Chi Ossé were also among those arrested.Inside the general assembly, dozens of envoys from across the world walked out as Netanyahu began his speech, where he assailed both enemies and allies that have crossed him in recent months, including Britain and France, which have recently moved to recognise the state of Palestine.UN delegates walk out as Benjamin Netanyahu prepares to address general assembly – video“They accuse Israel, tiny Israel, of colonialism – some colonialism. And who’s accusing us? Among them are people in Britain and in France.

articles.title: Iran awaiting response from Trump on proposal to open strait of Hormuz in six days
articles.excerpt: Iran said it has told Donald Trump it is willing to open the strait of Hormuz in six days, and to start talks on its nuclear program the day after, so long as the US lifts sanctions on Iran’s oil exports in return, ends the war on all fronts – including in Lebanon – and releases some of Iran’s frozen assets.The proposal is designed to accelerate the steps first laid down in the memorandum of understanding signed by the US and Iran in June, particularly by helping the talks on Iran’s nuclear program start much more quickly than previously agreed.Iran says a deal on the temporary route through the strait of Hormuz has been agreed with Oman, describing it as a done deal, and is ready to register the details with the International Maritime Organisation.Abbas Araghchi, the Iranian foreign minister, said he was waiting to hear a response from the Americans to the proposal. He added that he had consulted on the plan with China, which fully supported the proposal.Saudi Arabia had been expected to endorse the Oman-Iran route through the strait last week, but pulled back partly due to anger that Iranian-backed Houthis had started attacking Saudi Arabia as part of their dispute over the future of Yemen.Iran claims it has urged the Houthis to cease the attacks on Saudi Arabia but that it does not have control over Houthi decision-making.Araghchi, speaking to reporters in New York, said: “We have introduced a plan to the US through the mediators that if certain conditions are met, the strait will be open within seven days and talks will start.”He said the Iranian preconditions were not new, and were contained in the Islamabad memorandum of understanding that was signed by Trump.The advantage of the proposal, apart from opening the strait and lifting the chokehold on the world economy, would be bringing the US to the talks on Iran’s nuclear program much more quickly. Talks on the nuclear program under the MoU would not have started for 60 days.

articles.title: Takeaways from the Trump-Xi state visit: Pageantry and pandas
articles.excerpt: President Trump and Chinese President Xi Jinping (left) speak via an interpreter as they depart following a tour of the National Archives Museum in Washington, D.C., on Sept. 25. Win McNamee/Getty Images hide caption toggle caption Win McNamee/Getty Images President Trump rolled out the red carpet for Xi Jinping this week for the first state visit that the Chinese leader has made since 2015. The visit comes at an important time for both men. For Trump, the state visit comes about six weeks before the midterm elections. Xi has an important calendar ahead as well, with a key Communist Party meeting scheduled for next month that should set up a widely expected announcement next fall that Xi will rule for another five-year term. But there were a few commitments that came out of the meetings in Washington this week and more emphasis put on pageantry. Expectations were low for major takeaways The U.S. says the two countries will extend by two months a trade truce that lets the U.S. access rare earth elements from China, and for China to access some advanced American semiconductor chips. But the two delegations did not announce crucial details about two still-unformed boards of trade and investment, Boeing purchases and pending Chinese agricultural purchases. Instead, the two men relied on cordial remarks that glossed over the significant trade and economic complaints that have driven recent tension in the U.S.-China relationship. At a state dinner of about 145 guests, Xi toasted to Trump's health and a "new chapter" in bilateral relations, while Trump highlighted the long history of commerce between both countries. Xi "wielded many of the usual feel-good tropes of Chinese diplomacy," said Lucy Hornby, author of The Last Man, an upcoming biography on Xi, such as panda diplomacy. In his opening remarks, Trump referenced the intertwined histories of the U.S.

articles.title: There's a global pandemic treaty that's signed -- and in 'limbo.' What's the holdup?
articles.excerpt: These letters are part of the translated genetic code of the novel coronavirus that sparked the global pandemic. A new treaty aims to promote the sharing of such information among nations for any future virus that threatens the planet. Smith Collection/Gado//via Getty Images hide caption toggle caption Smith Collection/Gado//via Getty Images The World Health Organization adopted the pandemic agreement in May 2025, aimed at making the world better prepared for the next global health crisis — but countries were only able to get the votes because they agreed to kick the can on finalizing the most contentious details. That can kicking has continued for the past year and half. Countries met last week for the eighth round of negotiations in Geneva, but there was little to show for it. "The pandemic agreement is really in a state of continued limbo," says Suerie Moon, co-director of the global health center at the Geneva Graduate Institute. "The mood is somber, I think a lot of countries know we have to make progress, and yet the path forward is not obvious." At the center of the debate is access and equity — whether countries should be obligated to share data on new pathogens with the international community quickly, and what obligations countries have to share the vaccines, drugs or tests developed from those data. "There was staggering inequity during COVID-19, where rich countries had access to vaccines almost immediately, and were able to procure it multiple times over for their population," while lower-income countries got scraps, says Sangeeta Shashikant, a legal adviser for the Third World Network, a nonprofit. "The pandemic agreement is an attempt to bridge that gap." In principle, countries have agreed to these obligations. And they see them as crucial to having a system in place that allows for rapid response to the next pandemic in a more equitable way.

articles.title: Pope Leo warns a 'paradise of machines' could undermine humanity on his France visit
articles.excerpt: Pope Leo XIV and French President Emmanuel Macron attend a joint statement at the Élysée Palace in Paris, Friday. Teresa Suarez/AP hide caption toggle caption Teresa Suarez/AP PARIS — Pope Leo XIV warned Friday that a "paradise of machines" risked undermining humanity as he opened a trip to France by posing fundamental questions about what it means to be human in the age of artificial intelligence, a nuclear arms race and other threats to life itself. Leo raised existential concerns about scientific progress, life and human rights during his opening speech to President Emmanuel Macron and authorities at the Élysée Palace and then to diplomats and United Nations employees at the headquarters of UNESCO, the U.N. culture and education organization. With wars plaguing Europe and the Middle East, he reaffirmed the Vatican's opposition to nuclear weapons and said the nuclear deterrence doctrine was "mistaken" since it was just fueling a new arms race. "Peace is not a balance of power; rather, it is built day by day through dialogue and justice," he said. Leo has an intense four days in France, where the Catholic Church has lost ground on influencing ethical issues given the strict approach to secularism that is enshrined in the French Constitution. Church bells tolled across the country when Leo's charter flight landed at Paris' Orly airport, and more than a million people are expected to turn out to see him. They lined the streets of the capital as Leo's motorcade passed by, underscoring the surprising level of interest in Leo's visit, the first official state visit by a pope in 18 years. Macron said Leo's visit brings "a source of hope" to many French people. "France stands on the side of peace, effective multilateralism, respect for international law and the United Nations Charter ... because every life has equal value, and all peoples must be defended," he said.

articles.title: Former U.S. ambassador to China on Xi Jinping's visit to Washington
articles.excerpt: NPR's Leila Fadel speaks with former U.S. Ambassador to China Nicholas Burns about Chinese President Xi Jinping's visit to Washington and what has been accomplished. Transcript LEILA FADEL, HOST: OK. For more, let's bring in Nicholas Burns here. He was the United States ambassador to China from 2021 to 2025. He's now an international relations scholar at Harvard University. Good morning, ambassador. Welcome back to the program.NICHOLAS BURNS: Good morning, Leila.FADEL: So we just heard from our correspondent Deepa Shivaram that there was little in the way of grand bargains coming out of this much-trumpeted visit between - state visit between President Trump and President Xi. What, if anything, do you think the visit achieved?BURNS: You know, I think that the fact that they met is important. These are the two most important leaders in the world. This is our most difficult relationship in the world.FADEL: Yeah.BURNS: Highly challenged. And so we need our heads of government to be working together. I think it's been positive. This is the second meeting this year, perhaps two more in November and December. That's one, I think, benefit. The second is that Scott Bessent, the Treasury secretary, was able to negotiate with the Chinese. There's going to be a tariff truce and a supply chain truce. Neither side will continue that war through January of this year.Obviously, they want to extend it far beyond that. That would give our economic relationship some badly needed stability. So I think those are two benefits from this visit. I am, Leila, impressed in another way, maybe a more negative way, by the symbolism. You know, the American people want their president to be polite and civil to a foreign leader.FADEL: Yeah.BURNS: That just makes sense. But the over-the-top flattery by President Trump of President Xi - the red carpets, the pomp and circumstance, the marching bands - President Xi is not going to be swayed by that. He's highly intelligent, obviously.

articles.title: Netanyahu rages against critics, including Mamdani, at the U.N. General Assembly
articles.excerpt: Israeli Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu holds up a Starlink satellite internet dish as he speaks during the 81st session of the U.N. General Assembly at United Nations headquarters on Thursday. Seth Wenig/AP hide caption toggle caption Seth Wenig/AP Protesters rallied outside the United Nations building in New York and many delegates inside walked out of the room as Israeli Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu gave a fiery address to the General Assembly, denying allegations of genocide and slamming his critics, including the city's mayor, Zohran Mamdani. He called allegations of Israeli genocide in Gaza "the biggest lie of the century" and defended attacking Iran alongside the U.S., calling it "one of the easiest decisions I've ever had to make." He added: "if we hadn't done it, we'd all be dead." In his Thursday speech, he lashed out against the protesters outside — who included Hollywood stars Susan Sarandon and Hacks actress Hannah Einbinder, both detained during the anti-Netanyahu protest — calling them "phony" and asking why they hadn't all protested when Iranian security forces killed thousands of demonstrators in January. He also berated the dozens of U.N. delegates who walked out when he started his speech, calling them "moral cowards." Netanyahu then attacked Mayor Mamdani, who has called him a war criminal and pushed for federal authorities to act on the International Criminal Court-issued arrest warrant for him. The Israeli leader called Mamdani, New York's first Muslim mayor, "antisemitic." "Mr. Mamdani, you tried to stop me from coming here. You tried to silence me. Well, you can't silence me, and you can't silence the truth," Netanyahu said in his speech.

articles.title: Is Switzerland's neutrality at a crossroads?
articles.excerpt: A campaign poster urges Swiss voters to reject a neutrality initiative ahead of a Sept. 27 nationwide vote on whether to enshrine permanent armed neutrality in the constitution and limit participation in military alliances and sanctions. Fabrice Coffrini/AFP via Getty Images hide caption toggle caption Fabrice Coffrini/AFP via Getty Images BERN, Switzerland — The people of Switzerland are voting this weekend on whether to reinterpret their long tradition of neutrality. For more than 200 years, the Swiss have stayed out of wars. Their neutral status was originally imposed on them by the big 19th-century European powers; France on one side, and the Austro-Hungarian Empire on the other - which wanted a buffer zone between them. So, although not of their own choosing, neutrality allowed Switzerland to avoid the slaughter of two world wars, and, in later years, to use its neutral status to justify continuing its trade with repressive regimes, such as apartheid South Africa, that other governments had sanctioned. That changed in 2022 when Russia invaded Ukraine. After a few days' hesitation, Switzerland, which is not a member of the European Union, joined the EU's sanctions against Moscow, stopping trade, and freezing billions of dollars in Russian assets. The move was welcomed by many younger Swiss. As its government agonised over how to react, Switzerland's cities had seen days of protests calling for solidarity with Ukraine. But traditionalists were angry at what they saw as a weakening of neutrality. They collected the required signatures to force this weekend's nationwide vote, which would explicitly forbid Switzerland from joining economic sanctions unless they are approved by the UN Security Council – an unlikely prospect nowadays since the five permanent members (the U.S., China, Russia, France and the United Kingdom) agree on very little.

articles.title: Iran's president says his country has 'no trust' in U.S. in meeting with journalists
articles.excerpt: NPR's Steve Inskeep was part of a small group of journalists who met with an Iranian official on the sidelines of the U.N. General Assembly in New York. He tells Leila Fadel what he learned. Transcript LEILA FADEL, HOST: The president of Iran has spent much of this week in New York. It's a rare occasion, a president visiting a country while his nation is at war with it. Masoud Pezeshkian was here for the annual meeting of the United Nations, and he met with journalists yesterday, including our Steve Inskeep. Good morning, Steve.STEVE INSKEEP, BYLINE: Good morning.FADEL: So what did you get out of the session?INSKEEP: I felt that I got some insights into how Iran sees the effort to end this war. President Pezeshkian was with Abbas Araghchi, who is Iran's foreign minister. And he - Araghchi - is the diplomat who met with U.S. officials this week. So we got to hear a little bit from both. This started, I should tell you, as an off-the-record session with nobody to be quoted. But afterward, Iranian officials consented to put many comments on the record, so I can tell you a little bit about what was.FADEL: How do the Iranians see the talks?INSKEEP: They gave the impression that they were going through these talks without much optimism. The president said, quote, we have "no trust" in the United States since the U.S. has attacked Iran during negotiations before. He said Iran is only negotiating so the U.S. cannot claim that Iran is refusing to negotiate and is going for a bomb and so forth. The foreign minister said he met this week with two people who were close to President Trump - Trump's envoy Steve Witkoff and his son-in-law Jared Kushner. This was a three-hour meeting that was supposed to be secret, according to the Iranians, but then President Trump disclosed it, and that led to a public backlash in Iran where politicians say the foreign minister went beyond his instructions to have a meeting at all.FADEL: Oh, interesting.

articles.title: Former U.S. Ambassador to Israel on Netanyahu's speech at UNGA
articles.excerpt: NPR's Leila Fadel speaks with former U.S. Ambassador to Israel Thomas Nides about Israeli Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu's speech at the United Nations General Assembly. Transcript LEILA FADEL, HOST: For more on Israeli Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu's speech at the U.N., I'm joined now by Thomas Nides. He served as U.S. ambassador to Israel from 2021 to 2023. Ambassador, good morning and welcome to the program.THOMAS NIDES: Thank you for having me.FADEL: So diplomats streaming out of Netanyahu's speech in protest, hundreds of demonstrators outside saying he wasn't welcome. What did that tell you about attitudes towards Netanyahu on this global stage and in the United States?NIDES: Listen. It bums me out. Listen, I'm a - you know, as you know, I care deeply about the state of Israel. I obviously served there. I - you know, I'm proudly supportive of Israel, and I love the country. And it bums me out. I mean, the idea that, you know, these countries walk out - that's happened before. But I - obviously it's a much more extreme time right now. And I yearn for the time that we had, you know, just a few years ago. Think the last one was Prime Minister Lapid who gave a, you know, again, quote, normal speech. We are not, obviously, living in a normal time. But I want to get back to what Israel is - a democratic state - and for people to understand the beauty of the country. We are not there right now, and that speech certainly didn't reflect that.FADEL: Well, tell me more about that when you say - back to the time of a normal speech. What did you make of Netanyahu's tone and his remarks?NIDES: Listen. I mean, you know, there's a lot of theater. I mean, I am - listen. Again, you know, Israel is suffering. It's gone through the - October 7, the worst crisis since the Holocaust. They've been attacked by Iran. They've - attacked by Hezbollah and the Houthis. So I - to be clear, a lot of things can be true at the same time.

articles.title: Trump's state dinner for Xi features sea bass and a long list of tech titans
articles.excerpt: President Donald Trump shakes hands with China's President Xi Jinping in the East Room of the White House during a State Dinner, Thursday, Sept. 24, 2026, in Washington. Alex Brandon/AP hide caption toggle caption Alex Brandon/AP WASHINGTON — A tech-heavy guest list, the fashion choices of those on it, who sat where and what was on the menu marked the softer — often and glitzier — details of diplomacy as Donald Trump threw a Thursday night state dinner honoring China's leader Xi Jinping. The event featured a cavalcade of billionaires, Washington powerbrokers, business leaders and the type of festivities that most excite Trump, who has a reputation for reveling in hosting parties. "President Xi and I both understand we represent different systems, but the ties between our people endure, and we've never gotten along better," Trump said during his toast, adding that "together, we can continue to build a relationship that promotes prosperity and security for future generations." Trump has done his best to impress Xi during China's leader's during Xi's three-day visit to Washington, and praised their close personal relationship — even as he has decried top Democratic candidates as "communists" ahead of the November midterm elections. Xi and Trump discussed tensions over Taiwan, trade and artificial intelligence during business hours — even as an ongoing First Amendment fight over press access at the White House has unfolded. But Trump publicly chose to focus on showing Xi his White House updates on Thursday afternoon, including letting him tour his Marine One presidential helicopter and a new helipad he built for it — before attention quickly turned to the flashy details of the swanky meal. Xi noted in his own toast that "President Trump has pledged to make America great again" and that "China is committed to achieving great national rejuvenation." "These two goals are both ambitious and can surely be mutually reinforcing," Xi said.

articles.title: 每升减税17欧分 德国联邦议院通过新的“燃油补贴”计划
articles.url: https://www.dw.com/zh/每升减税17欧分-德国联邦议院通过新的-燃油补贴-计划/a-79435013?maca=chi-rss-chi-all-1127-rdf
articles.excerpt: （德国之声中文网）德国大联合政府提出一项法案，从今年10月到12月底，每升柴油和汽油的能源税降低14欧分，计入相应减免的增值税后，每升燃油总共减税17欧分。 在本周五（9月25日）德国联邦议院举行的记名投票中，562名议员中有434人对该法案投了赞成票，128人投了反对票。该法案现已通过快速程序提交联邦参议院表决，以确保补贴能于10月1日生效。 整体纾困方案规模约25亿欧元 该方案将导致国家损失25亿欧元的税收。由此产生的负担将由联邦政府和各州政府共同分担。为了缓解因伊朗战争导致油价飙升所带来的冲击，德国春季时已实施过为期两个月的“燃油折扣”。 基民盟财政政策专家斯特凡·科尔巴赫（Stefan Korbach）表示，高昂的燃油价格给普通家庭和企业都带来沉重负担，燃油补贴是“当前能迅速实施的最佳手段”，能产生“立竿见影”的效果，并有助于抑制通货膨胀。他也指出，尽管该措施仅是“权宜之计”，无法根除问题，但对于当前局势而言，它仍是最佳的可用手段。 在议会辩论中，社民党议会党团副主席阿尔芒·佐恩（Armand Zorn）称各方就该草案进行“艰难的讨论”，但鉴于柴油和汽油价格大幅飙升，实施“燃油折扣”的决定将为民众的日常生活提供即时缓解。执政联盟还就“燃油价格上限”达成了一致，旨在限制石油公司提价的空间。伊朗战争推高油价 德国经济雪上加霜To view this video please enable JavaScript, and consider upgrading to a web browser that supports HTML5 video 绿党：“荒谬的解决方案” 绿党、左翼党和德国选择党等反对党对该法案提出了尖锐批评。绿党议会党团主席卡塔琳娜·德勒格（Katharina Dröge）将这一临时减税措施形容为“荒谬的解决方案”。她指出，此前5月和6月推出的“燃油折扣”就并未完全惠及消费者，且该措施的成本相当于联邦预算中一年内削减的所有家庭福利的总额。 专家批评该措施缺乏节油激励 此前，多个环保和社会组织已对这项燃油纾困措施表达了批评意见。德国经济研究所（DIW）的经济学家克劳迪娅·肯费特（Claudia Kemfert）称这是应对高能源价格的错误举措，并指出该措施针对性差、成本高昂，且无法鼓励人们节约燃油。肯费特认为，这实际上是在补贴对化石燃料的依赖，对于气候保护而言是“朝着错误方向迈出的一步”。 创记录：32国释放4亿桶原油储备To view this video please enable JavaScript, and consider upgrading to a web browser that supports HTML5 video （德新社等） DW中文有Instagram！欢迎搜寻dw.chinese，看更多深入浅出的图文与影音报道。 © 2026年德国之声版权声明：本文所有内容受到著作权法保护，如无德国之声特别授权，不得擅自使用。任何不当行为都将导致追偿，并受到刑事追究。

articles.title: “背后支持习近平的，是中国的综合国力”
articles.url: https://www.dw.com/zh/背后支持习近平的，是中国的综合国力/a-79432798?maca=chi-rss-chi-all-1127-rdf
articles.excerpt: （德国之声中文网）美国总统特朗普高规格接待习近平的报道和画面传回到中国，美联社记者走访了北京市的一些市民，他们认为，可以借此看到中国的地位在提升。 在北京读研的项子宇（音）告诉美联社，“我读到新闻说，美国对习主席的接待标准非常高”，“这给我留下很深的印象，这表明，我们国家已经变得很强大了”，“因为背后支持他的，是中国的综合国力。” 美联社街头采访的几位人士，基本都持这样的观点，至于中国媒体更是盛赞中美合作。 周五（9月25日）中国社媒平台上，三个最靠前的热搜话题是：特朗普和习近平的会谈、习近平和彭丽媛出席白宫国宴，以及习近平在中秋节之际向中国人民致以问候。 北京居民沈佐航（音）说，“我们不要贸易战，没有军事冲突。即使在台湾问题上，我们也正在朝着好的方向发展，而不是激烈对抗。”他认为，“双方正在以更加缓和与默许的方式处理问题。” 中国外交部在新闻稿报道，习近平在同特朗普的会谈中，呼吁美国反对台独，希望华盛顿谨慎处理这一问题。特朗普尚未对台湾话题发表评论，但此前曾表示过，愿意与中国就对台军售进行谈判。 一名姓向的大学生对美联社表示，这次峰会释放了积极信号，有利于改善中国公众对两国关系的看法。“这比不沟通要好”，他说。 “台湾这个筹码越来越低” 路透社周五在北京一个公园进行了访问。 一名在教育领域工作的高姓男子说，“中美两国携手一定更好。但中国的崛起对美国有一定威胁，所以美国对中国还会有各方面的压制。但这些年来，中国发展越来越快，美国未必能压制住中国。” 在出版界工作的姓周男子谈了他对AI管控的看法：“人工智能应该有一个合理的框架，尤其在美国公司爆出人工智能失控、攻击别国公司之后。昨天爆出攻击了澳大利亚政府网站。美国在人工智能处于领先地位，他制定框架也可能旨在限制中国人工智能的发展。所以我们要有清醒的认识。” 同台湾关系的问题上，这名周姓男子也谈了自己的看法，“中国强大了，台湾这个筹码的价值越来越低，美国不如拿它换取一些对美国自身有利的东西。” 民众对习近平访美的期待 还在习近平抵达华盛顿之前，法新社记者在北京随机访问了几名路人。 一名黄姓男子在北京市中心对法新社说，这次访问对于塑造这两个全球最大的经济体之间的关系至关重要。“作为一名普通公民，我希望中美关系能够实现长期、稳定且互利共赢的发展。”他还表示，“我也希望通过习主席对美国的访问，以及与特朗普总统之间友好、和谐且充满善意的沟通，我们能够推动双边关系的发展。” 在金融界工作的陆浩（音）表示，他正密切关注会谈后是否达成任何经济协议。他还记得，贸易战期间自己与客户所经历的艰难时刻。27岁的他告诉法新社，“我真心希望这次访问能释放积极信号，为全球股市带来更多利好消息。”他说，“因为（贸易战）一打响，我们的股市就首当其冲，遭受最严重的冲击。”他表示，“很清楚，贸易战带来双输的局面。” 从事外贸服务行业的Lucy Lu也告诉法新社，大国之间的冲突“对各方都有害”。43岁的她表示，由于关税上调，出口企业的某些商品，变得极难运出。“我真心希望各国在关税问题上，能保持友好的态度。”中国和台湾民众如何看待“习特高峰会”To view this video please enable JavaScript, and consider upgrading to a web browser that supports HTML5 video DW中文有Instagram！欢迎搜寻dw.chinese，看更多深入浅出的图文与影音报道。 © 2026年德国之声版权声明：本文所有内容受到著作权法保护，如无德国之声特别授权，不得擅自使用。任何不当行为都将导致追偿，并受到刑事追究。

articles.title: 德语媒体： 中美博弈 - 谁能笑到最后？
articles.url: https://www.dw.com/zh/德语媒体：-中美博弈-谁能笑到最后？/a-79432942?maca=chi-rss-chi-all-1127-rdf
articles.excerpt: 德语媒体： 中美博弈 - 谁能笑到最后？图像来源: Evan Vucci/REUTERS（德国之声中文网）《法兰克福汇报》就华盛顿特习会发表评论写道，特朗普总统喜欢以羞辱和威胁手段对待美国的传统盟友，但对于中国领导人习近平的来访，这位美国总统却刻意摆出极大的敬意，并以“伟大领袖”和“朋友”称呼这位共产党领导人。但除此之外，中美双方并没有达成实质性的政治协议吗。这篇题为《习近平只是在逢场作戏》的评论写道： “特朗普之所以要避免同中国发生正面冲突，原因有很多：首先，这位美国总统喜欢以其自恋视角来看待国际政治，尤其喜欢外人的讨好和奉承。特朗普认为，他同各大国领导人的私人友谊，足以左右世界政治。而习近平和普京则对此暗自发笑。毕竟习近平和普京都很清楚各自的战略利益，他们只是和特朗普‘逢场作戏’，试图操控这位西方阵营曾经的领导人。 其次，特朗普刚一开始其第二个总统任期，就遭遇了习近平的下马威。作为坚定的贸易保护主义者，特朗普在其内阁对华鹰派的鼓动之下，发起了针对中国的贸易战。但中国领导人习近平对此早已准备，立即叫停了对美国的稀土出口。特朗普很快就败下阵来，此前宣布的关税也基本全盘收回。习近平让特朗普意识到，美国总统的权力也是有界限的。这一次双方还在华盛顿就延长休战期做出了安排。” 《法兰克福汇报》评论认为，北京凭借稀土等筹码迫使美国在贸易战中主动退让，而伊朗战争又令美国无暇他顾，因此特朗普在对华问题上变得越来越“谨言慎行”，这一点在台湾问题上表现的尤为突出： “事实上，特朗普当局在尽力避免谈及台湾问题，并已推迟就一项价值140亿美元的对台军售案做出决定。显然，特朗普总统的确很重视习近平就台湾问题发出的警告。习近平曾表示，任何在涉台问题的错误举动，都将会带来危险的后果。此前，特朗普甚至称这项旨在加强台湾防空能力的对台军售案是同北京谈判的筹码。这种言论想必会在台北引起极大的担忧，毕竟这等于赋予了习近平在对台军售问题上的发言权。法兰克福汇报：特朗普总统的确很重视习近平就台湾问题发出的警告。图像来源: Alex Brandon/AP Photo/picture alliance 一旦台湾遭遇危险，特朗普是否会出手相助，安全问题专家们对此普遍表示怀疑。因为，特朗普对美国利益的定义非同以往。盟友关系本来是美国作为超级大国的特殊优势，但特朗普对此显然不屑一顾。 当然，特朗普并没有低估习近平的野心。这一点在有关人工智能的讨论中也得到了充分体现。特朗普拒绝对人工智能研发进行管控，也并没有隐瞒他这样做的动机：‘谁嬴了人工智能，谁就赢得了一切。’这位美国总统不愿放弃美国高科技企业在该领域取得的领先地位，也深知中国正在快速追赶。而这同样也是一种不信任的表现：特朗普并不认为中国会出于伦理考量放慢人工智能的研发速度。人工智能已经成为中美博弈的新战场。中美冲突只是被推迟了而已。” “这是一个双雄鼎立的时代” 对于中国党和国家领导人习近平的美国之行，《新苏黎世报》评论写道，中美两国围绕经济、科技、能源和地缘政治的竞争非但没有减弱，而且会长期持续： “没有任何一方拥有绝对优势：美国在一些核心领域领先，中国则在另一些领域表现出色。美国无可争议的主导地位已经成为过去。但这并不意味着中国能够取代美国，成为新的世界霸主。更确切地说，这是一个双雄鼎立的时代，双方都有能力让对方的计划落空，但却没有任何一方强大到足以迫使对方接受自己制定的游戏规则。也正因为如此，制定‘战略稳定’框架就显得更为重要了。如果没有这样的防护栏，擦枪走火导致冲突升级的风险就将越来越高。未来几年内，中美竞争将对世界产生深刻影响。 就目前而言，中美双方仍愿意开展对话。习近平飞抵华盛顿时，特朗普亲赴机场迎接。特朗普很擅长以这种作秀的方式展示友好姿态，而习近平也愿意予以配合。这是他们两人之间的一场游戏，他们也都确信，自己将是笑到最后的那一位。” 摘编自其他媒体的内容，不代表德国之声的立场或观点。 DW中文有Instagram！欢迎搜寻dw.chinese，看更多深入浅出的图文与影音报道。 © 2026年德国之声版权声明：本文所有内容受到著作权法保护，如无德国之声特别授权，不得擅自使用。任何不当行为都将导致追偿，并受到刑事追究。

articles.title: 长平观察：特朗普在错误的赛道中一路狂奔
articles.url: https://www.dw.com/zh/长平观察：特朗普在错误的赛道中一路狂奔/a-79431554?maca=chi-rss-chi-all-1127-rdf
articles.excerpt: 时评人长平指出，此前拜登对习近平的“红线”并没有买账。但是，这一次习近平大可放心，特朗普自己对民主人权毫无兴趣。图为特朗普9月24日在白宫设晚宴招待习近平图像来源: Evelyn Hockstein/REUTERS（德国之声中文网）周三（9月23日），习近平启程前往华盛顿的当天，《人民日报》刊出中国驻美大使谢锋的署名文章《推动中美建设性战略稳定关系落地落实》。文章写道：“台湾问题、民主人权、道路制度、发展权利四条红线不容挑战。” 第二天，一群中国记者被放进白宫采访，而CNN、MS NOW和《政治新闻网》（Politico）的记者一度被挡在门外——特朗普以“国家安全威胁”为由下令阻拦，尽管法院已裁定其违法。据报道，特朗普当天还称，中国人有“最友好的记者团”。 据CNN报道，习近平夫妇抵达时，直播画面里隐约传来门外抗议者的喊声：“释放所有政治犯！”这是白宫这一整天里，唯一出现人权的地方。 多个团体在白宫周边和中国大使馆外发起抗议，高喊“让西藏自由”、“让香港自由”、“停止对维吾尔人的种族灭绝”、“让台湾保持自由”以及“释放黎智英”等口号。这些喊声被阻挡在特朗普对习近平高规格宴会之外。 “民主人权”作为红线，到底在禁止谈什么？ 谢锋的文章受到外媒普遍的重视。事实上，从标题到内容，没有一句是这位大使自己说的话。文章说，今年5月，习近平同特朗普在北京会晤，“达成的最重要政治共识就是确定了中美建设性战略稳定关系的新定位”。 至于“四条红线”，据中国外交部发言人介绍，早在2022年11月巴厘岛会晤中，习近平就向美国总统拜登强调过；2024年11月的利马会晤，他再次提出。据新华社报道，原话是：“台湾问题、民主人权、道路制度、发展权利是中方的4条红线，不容挑战。” 民主人权首先是国内人民的基本权利，一个政权竟然理直气壮地把它设定为不可碰触的红线，这是多么荒唐而又残暴的现实。 例如，今年6月，谢锋在美中贸易全国委员会的晚宴上再次强调这“四条红线”，还补充说：“当中国的拉布布不必戴上所谓‘强迫劳动’的帽子……” 他所指的是，国际劳工权益组织“中国劳工观察”（China Labor Watch）今年1月发布的一份调查报告。报告调查了风靡全球的玩具“拉布布”在中国的生产工厂存在一系列突出问题，包括：严重超出法定上限的加班工时、大量使用劳务派遣工、不透明的劳动合同安排、疑似规避社会保险缴纳、缺乏充分的安全培训以及职业健康与安全防护的明显缺失等。而且，该工厂没有工会或有效的申诉机制，并有大量工人反映管理层存在霸凌行为、言语性骚扰，以及对宿舍和食堂卫生条件的担忧。 难道这些工人不都是中国人吗？民主人权作为红线“不容挑战”的意思就是，这些中国人活该遭受剥削和欺侮，谁也别来过问。谁是特朗普最喜欢的独裁者？ 拜登对习近平的红线并没有买账。2022年巴厘岛会晤，根据白宫发布的纪要，他就新疆、西藏和香港的做法以及更广泛的人权问题表达关切；2024年利马会晤，他“指出人权的重要性以及所有国家尊重其人权承诺的责任”。 但是，这一次习近平大可放心，特朗普自己对民主人权毫无兴趣。 密西西比州共和党参议员、参议院军事委员会主席罗杰·威克（Roger Wicker）提醒说：“在每一分钟的对话中，我们的三军统帅都应该牢记，他的客人是一名残暴、未经选举产生、实行压迫统治的独裁者，他试图支配邻国，而且其庞大的军事武库直接瞄准美利坚合众国。” 令人遗憾的是，他的“三军统帅”正在社交媒体上低三下四地称颂“备受尊敬的中国国家主席”，并恭维“他美丽的妻子彭女士”。他还希望以类似的方式接待被国际刑事法院以战争罪通缉的普京（Vladimir Putin），已邀请后者出席今年12月在迈阿密举行的二十国集团峰会。 除了反反复复公开谄媚习近平和普京之外，《纽约时报》首席白宫记者彼得·贝克（Peter Baker）还列举了特朗普对其他独裁者、暴君与威权统治者的亲近：他对朝鲜的金正恩表白“我们坠入了爱河”，称埃及的阿卜杜勒-法塔赫·塞西（Abdel Fattah el-Sisi）是“我最喜欢的独裁者”，对沙特阿拉伯的穆罕默德·本·萨勒曼（Mohammed bin Salman）说“我太喜欢他了”，土耳其的埃尔多安（Recep Tayyip Erdoğan）则是“我的一个非常好的朋友”，萨尔瓦多的布克尔（Nayib Bukele）也是“一位了不起的总统”。

articles.title: “G2”峰会：特朗普超规格款待习近平
articles.url: https://www.dw.com/zh/g2-峰会：特朗普超规格款待习近平/a-79430234?maca=chi-rss-chi-all-1127-rdf
articles.excerpt: （德国之声中文网）在受到特朗普夫妇亲自抵达机场迎接的罕见礼遇后，习近平在对美国进行国事访问的第二日（9月24日）和夫人彭丽媛一同前往白宫，再次受到极为隆重的欢迎。 特朗普与习近平在欢迎仪式上分别致辞并检阅仪仗队，观看美军刺枪表演。习近平表示，未来5年将邀请10万名美国青少年赴中国交流学习，并宣布近期大熊猫“平平”和“福双”将落户美国南部佐治亚州亚特兰大动物园。 不过，尽管白宫通过视频网站等平台直播欢迎仪式，美国各大电视台却都没有对此进行直播，以抗议特朗普政府禁止CNN等三家媒体进入白宫。据美媒报道，直到接近中午，CNN等三家媒体的记者才获准进入白宫。24日当天，一名联邦法官暂时叫停了白宫对CNN等三家美国媒体发出的“禁入令”。特朗普夫妇在白宫欢迎习近平夫妇来访图像来源: RS/MPI/Capital Pictures/picture alliance 谈了什么？ 欢迎仪式后，习近平与特朗普举行了约三小时会晤。据中国官方报道，在双边会谈中，习近平称要“朝着合作为主、竞争有度、分歧可控、和平可期的方向努力，走出一条两个大国的正确相处之道”，并“希望美方坚持反对‘台独 ’的正确立场，慎重处理台湾问题，为中美战略合作和两国关系发展奠定坚实基础。” 外界此前预计，习近平在访问中会向特朗普施压，要求其停止对台军售。特朗普在5月访华后曾表示，他暂缓了一项价值约140亿美元的对台军售计划，并称之为“非常好的谈判筹码”。此举引发了美国在亚洲的一些盟友、甚至特朗普所在共和党内部分人士的担忧。他们担心特朗普可能会为了换取经济利益而削弱华盛顿对台北的支持。 美中领导人于华盛顿举行会晤前夕，中国驻美大使谢锋撰文称“中美合作则双赢，对抗则双输”，“中国的主权、安全和发展利益不容侵犯，台湾问题、民主人权、道路制度、发展权利四条红线不容挑战“。特朗普及内阁要员在白宫会晤习近平一行图像来源: Evan Vucci/REUTERS 中国官方报道还称，习近平表示，“双方可以继续开展人工智能对话，就其风险和收益进行交流，共同防范人工智能被滥用恶用”。此外，“两国元首还就中东局势、乌克兰危机、朝鲜半岛等重大国际和地区问题交换了意见”。特朗普近日称美国对伊朗问题正处于“决策阶段”，中国则表达了“鼓励伊朗和美国保持理性和克制”，重构谈判机制，进行实质性磋商的立场。但几乎没有迹象表明，北京愿意向伊朗施压，促使其满足美国的要求。 白宫尚未发布关于特朗普与习近平白宫会谈的官方摘要。中国官方报道称：“特朗普表示，习近平主席这次对美国的国事访问是一次伟大的访问。美中都是大国，我同习近平主席是好朋友，保持着深入密切沟通。在我们的领导下，美中关系一定能搞好。” 曾任白宫负责东亚事务主任、现就职于战略与国际问题研究中心（CSIS）的埃德加·卡根（Edgard Kagan）认为，习近平和特朗普截然不同的言辞基调反映了其不同的策略：“特朗普总统将此次会晤很大程度上定性为他与习近平之间的个人关系。有趣的是，习近平的态度则谨慎得多。他暗示这更多是关于国家间的关系，而非个人私交。” 习近平到访华盛顿当天，美国财政部长贝森特宣布，美中已同意将贸易休战协议延长两个月。这可能意味着中国将推迟原定于11月10日起实施的对稀土出口进行更严格限制的计划。 精英云集的晚宴与白宫外的抗议声 9月24日晚特朗普在白宫东厅为习近平夫妇举行的欢迎国宴也体现了特朗普热衷仪式感与奢华、崇尚财富与精英，不拘泥于传统礼仪的风格。 白宫公布的晚宴菜单包括黄南瓜浓汤、芝麻脆皮海鲈鱼和香草黄油慕斯配白宫蜂蜜冰激淋。祝酒时选用了1972年尼克松访华时使用的同款气泡酒。晚宴大厅的装饰突出了中国历史文化中红色的喜庆意义，以红色桌布，红色大丽花等致敬中国文化，同时搭配白宫珍藏的里根国宴镀金银器。 晚宴上美国亿万富翁、知名企业CEO云集，包括多位科技大腕，如苹果公司的库克（Tim Cook）、亚马逊的贝索斯（Jeff Bezos）、Alphabet的桑达尔·皮查伊（Sundar Pichai）、OpenAI的萨姆·奥特曼（Sam Altman）、特斯拉的马斯克（Elon Musk）以及英伟达的黄仁勋（Jensen Huang）。不过，近日高调警告人工智能风险的企业Anthropic代表没有露面。

articles.title: 白宫大迎宾客 抗议者呼声震天
articles.url: https://www.dw.com/zh/白宫大迎宾客-抗议者呼声震天/a-79427410?maca=chi-rss-chi-all-1127-rdf
articles.excerpt: （德国之声中文网）人们聚集在拉斐特公园（Lafayette Park）沿线的围栏后，挥舞旗帜，举着标语牌。扩音器将他们的呼喊声传播开来，公园的每一个角落都能听到，毗邻的白宫北门廊（North Portico）也不例外，而那里，仪仗队和红地毯已准备就绪，就等着宾客们前来出席国宴。 白宫欢迎仪式开始的时候，这边抗议者一遍又一遍高呼“习近平下台”、“可耻！习近平可耻！”等口号。 在中国驻美大使馆外，周四上午也聚集了抗议者，之后，他们游行到国会山附近。那里，许多人挥舞着西藏旗帜，高呼“西藏自由”的口号，也有人举着印有“自由”和“民主”、“保持台湾自由”、“光复香港，时代革命”等字样的标语牌。前众议院议长佩洛西参加了自由西藏组织的活动并做了发言，称让民选官员、美国总统和中国国家主席，听到抗议者的声音非常重要。 周四当天，华盛顿也出现支持中共的活动。数百人聚集在习近平下榻的酒店外，挥舞中美两国国旗，高呼“欢迎，欢迎，热烈欢迎”。他们打出的横幅上写着“热烈欢迎习近平主席访美”等字样。 支持习近平者图像来源: Alex Wroblewski/AFP 抗议中共领导人到访的活动在西方并不罕见，事实上，几乎每次都会伴随着这类活动。人们还记得2006年时任中国国家主席的胡锦涛在白宫致答谢词时，一名持大纪元记者证的女记者突然大喊：“布什总统，请阻止这个人。”“胡主席，您的时间是有限的。”她还呼喊了法轮功的口号。接着，这名女性被保安人员带走。布什总统立即向胡锦涛表示道歉。据称，中国电视台把这一段转播删除了，代之以“黑屏”。 DW中文有Instagram！欢迎搜寻dw.chinese，看更多深入浅出的图文与影音报道。 © 2026年德国之声版权声明：本文所有内容受到著作权法保护，如无德国之声特别授权，不得擅自使用。任何不当行为都将导致追偿，并受到刑事追究。

articles.title: 中国第一夫人彭丽媛在华府展示个人魅力
articles.url: https://www.dw.com/zh/中国第一夫人彭丽媛在华府展示个人魅力/a-79427423?maca=chi-rss-chi-all-1127-rdf
articles.excerpt: （德国之声中文网）在中国领导人习近平访问华盛顿之际，他的夫人彭丽媛发挥了“软实力”王牌的作用，展现出一个更温和、更亲切的中国形象。 周四，在华盛顿史密森尼国立亚洲艺术博物馆，合唱团的孩子们在演唱中国民歌《茉莉花》后，向她致意：“谢谢彭妈妈！” 中国驻美大使谢锋在社交平台X上强调了她的外交角色，并发布了一段彭丽媛为演出鼓掌的视频。 谢锋写道，彭丽媛“鼓励美国青少年继续学习中国语言和文化，成为中美友谊的使者”。 总部位于北京的咨询公司“策纬咨询”（Trivium China）的地缘政治分析师马祖尔（Joe Mazur）对路透社表示：“她让原本可能显得严肃甚至强硬的外交活动更具亲和力，并为中美关系营造一些令人愉悦的时刻。” 中国”第一夫人“通常保持低调 不过在中国社交媒体上，关于彭丽媛此行活动及着装风格的讨论受到严格限制。在中国，高层领导人个人生活等内容属于敏感话题。 路透社报道指出，在中国社交平台“小红书”上，搜索关于彭丽媛着装品味以及英语能力的内容，未显示任何结果。 路透社报道指出，彭丽媛端庄优雅的形象，为中美互动增添了一抹不同于传统外交的色彩。图为9月24日的白宫晚宴图像来源: Evelyn Hockstein/REUTERS 过去几十年来，中国高层领导人的夫人们通常保持低调，这在一定程度上和毛泽东夫人江青过往经历有关。 在文革期间，江青从幕后走向台前，不仅频繁高调亮相，还直接出任中共核心要职，成为“四人帮”主要成员。 在文革结束后，江青在狱中自尽，中共将“夫人干政”总结为“导致国家政治动荡的重大教训之一”。此后几届领导人的夫人均在公众面前尽量保持低调。 中国网民的“彭麻麻” 不过，随着彭丽媛成为“第一夫人”，这一情况有所改变。作为中国最广为人知的女高音歌唱家，中国媒体在报道她的活动时也获得了更大的空间。许多中国网民也亲切地称她为“彭麻麻”（彭妈妈的谐音）。 “他回到家时，我从未觉得家里来了一位领导人。在我眼中，他只是我的丈夫，”彭丽媛在2007年接受一家官媒采访时说道。她形容习近平生活简朴、工作勤奋且为人务实。 路透社的报道称，彭丽媛多年来一直致力于倡导关注艾滋病感染者等充满挑战的社会公益事业。 彭丽媛出身于普通家庭，因为出类拔萃的嗓音进入部队文工团。早在与习近平结婚前，她已经是中国家喻户晓的歌唱演员。她是习近平的第二任妻子，两人育有一女（习明泽）。 DW中文有Instagram！欢迎搜寻dw.chinese，看更多深入浅出的图文与影音报道。 © 2026年德国之声版权声明：本文所有内容受到著作权法保护，如无德国之声特别授权，不得擅自使用。任何不当行为都将导致追偿，并受到刑事追究。

articles.title: 德语媒体：暗流涌动的中美关系
articles.url: https://www.dw.com/zh/德语媒体：暗流涌动的中美关系/a-79416022?maca=chi-rss-chi-all-1127-rdf
articles.excerpt: 商报：盛大欢迎场面的背后，中美竞争关系正在不断激化图像来源: Saul Loeb/AFP（德国之声中文网）《商报》评论认为，尽管美国总统特朗普喜欢对习近平以“朋友”相称，但中美领导人之间绝不是什么“朋友”关系，精心安排的欢迎场面也无法改变这一事实。这篇题为《暗流涌动的中美竞争》的评论写道： “盛大欢迎场面的背后，中美竞争关系正在不断激化。两国间的矛盾虽然简单，却极具爆炸性：中国希望扩展自己的势力范围，先是在亚洲，进而要扩展至全球。但美国并不愿意将自己的影响力拱手相让。除此之外，为了扩大影响力，并支撑本国经济，中国凭借其规模庞大、并受到国家补贴的过剩产能，对各主要竞争对手形成了强劲的压力，这其中也包括美国。 而真正的危险却在于，面对这一巨大挑战，特朗普却没有任何的对华战略。这位总统喜欢凭直觉行事，他重视股市波动，更相信凭借个人关系，能让所有问题都迎刃而解。也正因为如此，他非常重视此次习近平的来访，当然也是因为与习的会晤也会提升他本人的声誉。 与前任拜登不同，特朗普在制定对华政策时，并不会同德国等长期盟友进行沟通协调，虽然协调一致的对华政策本来会具有更强的杀伤力。对欧洲来说，特朗普缺乏明确战略以及在对华问题上的单方行动，无疑是一个问题。因为特朗普的行为令人无法预测中美两国关系的未来走势，更无法判断这一切将会对欧洲产生怎样的影响。” 中国国家主席习近平抵达华盛顿数小时之后，美国财长贝森特就宣布，美中两国已同意将贸易休战期延长两个月。《商报》写道，显然两国领导人都不愿意让贸易战进一步升级，损害本国的经济增长： “但一旦两国关系层面上发生突发事件，导致贸易战死灰复燃又该如何呢？ 届时德国企业可能又要苦等来自中国的稀土材料了。北京此前就已经使用过这样的手段。欧洲人为了自身利益，也应当减少对中华人民共和国的依赖。与此同时，欧洲还应保护本土市场，免受中国高额补贴产品的冲击。或许从自由市场理念的层面来看，这类措施会令人感到痛苦，但有一点却是可以肯定的，美国人也会这么做。” “中美间存在严重的不信任” 《科隆城市报》客座评论认为，中美之间仍存在着根深蒂固的相互不信任，虽然双边关系出现缓和迹象，但这也只是基于利益考量的权宜之计： “中美两大国之间，仍充满了相互的不信任。中国对美国的权势地位仍有某种程度的尊重和认可，尽管认可度已经在逐步下降。而与此同时，美国则仍习惯性地将中国、而不是俄罗斯视为头号敌人。无论是在国会，还是民间，对中国极大的不信任感仍普遍存在。科隆城市报：特朗普意识到，习近平是一位必须高度重视的对手。图像来源: Alex Brandon/AP Photo/picture alliance 特朗普当年首次当选总统，某种程度上也是得益于他对中国的妖魔化。他指责中国是新冠疫情的源头，声称中国以巨额顺差强奸美国，并试图最终夺取美国世界头号经济强国的地位。第二个总统任期开始后，特朗普仍会公开表达他对中国的担忧。2025年，他曾一度对中国产品实施145%的关税，不过，这一关税很快就被大幅下调。因为，北京也对美国产品开始征收高额关税，并同时大规模限制关键矿产品的对美出口，从而使包括汽车、军火在内的众多美国工业领域受到严重冲击。特朗普很快就做出了让步。 此后，中美关系出现缓解趋势。特朗普终于意识到，习近平是一位必须高度重视的对手，他不像大多数欧洲人那样，可以任意摆布。 2025年10月，特朗普与习近平在韩国釜山举行了不到两小时的会谈，并签署了一份有效期一年的贸易协定。美国方面宣布，将对中国产品的平均关税从57%下调至47%，并在一年期限内暂停征收惩罚性关税。作为回报，中国方面承诺暂停针对稀土和其他高科技产品的出口管制，并增加从美国进口大豆及其他农产品的数量。... 一般认为，习近平此次访美行程将相对和谐。毕竟中美两国经济形势均欠佳，中国的青年失业率居高不下，而美国则是通胀率不断飙升，特朗普和习近平除了延长贸易停火，也别无选择。” 摘编自其他媒体的内容，不代表德国之声的立场或观点。 DW中文有Instagram！欢迎搜寻dw.chinese，看更多深入浅出的图文与影音报道。 © 2026年德国之声版权声明：本文所有内容受到著作权法保护，如无德国之声特别授权，不得擅自使用。任何不当行为都将导致追偿，并受到刑事追究。

articles.title: 泽连斯基：普京是散布战争思想的“零号病人”
articles.url: https://www.dw.com/zh/泽连斯基：普京是散布战争思想的-零号病人/a-79415420?maca=chi-rss-chi-all-1127-rdf
articles.excerpt: （德国之声中文网）在纽约联合国大会的辩论中，乌克兰总统泽连斯基就俄罗斯对国际社会构成的威胁发出严厉警告。他不仅描述了乌克兰在长达四年半的俄罗斯侵略战争中所承受的重负，还指出普京治下的俄罗斯对摩尔多瓦、波兰和波罗的海三国（立陶宛、拉脱维亚和爱沙尼亚）构成的威胁。 泽连斯基指出，莫斯科不尊重南高加索和中亚国家的独立。叙利亚和非洲多国也都曾遭受过“俄罗斯的暴行”。此外，俄罗斯帮助朝鲜发展军事技术，对亚洲邻国构成越来越大的威胁。 泽连斯基用一个医学术语形容普京说：“他是零号病人，战争思想正从他那里不断扩散。” 他说，普京正在让世界变得更加危险。“因此，必须阻止零号病人，剥夺他行动及散播邪恶的空间。” 泽连斯基指责普京是扩散战争思想的“零号病人”图像来源: Vyacheslav Prokofyev/Sputnik/AP Photo/dpa/picture alliance 泽连斯基再次请求提供防空导弹 与此同时，泽连斯基重申，乌克兰在应对这一威胁方面依赖国际援助，迫切需要防空武器。 他还介绍了乌克兰在无人机技术方面取得的进展。目前，乌克兰正与合作伙伴分享这些技术。泽连斯基说：“这不仅仅是出售无人机的问题，而是要与其他国家合作，建立一个现代化的、一体化的防御系统，以应对空中、海上和陆地上的无人机威胁。”他同时宣布与芬兰达成了无人机协议，并与澳大利亚达成了新的防务协议。 人口约300万的基辅近日来一直是俄罗斯无人机袭击的重点目标。此外，俄罗斯还针对乌克兰的能源，电力系统发动导弹袭击。DW专访泽连斯基：愿去美国见普京To view this video please enable JavaScript, and consider upgrading to a web browser that supports HTML5 video 拉夫罗夫：袭击不会停止 俄罗斯外长拉夫罗夫则在纽约联合国安理会会议上断然拒绝了西方提出的在对乌克兰战争中停火的提议。拉夫罗夫：“我们不会停止我们的特殊军事行动。” 拉夫罗夫说：“只有欧洲才希望暂停战争，以便‘趁此机会向乌克兰输送武器’。” 德国外长：俄罗斯的混合攻击已升级 德国外长瓦德富尔也在联合国安理会谈到了俄罗斯对乌克兰的侵略战争。他说：“俄罗斯对支持乌克兰和国际法的国家的混合攻击已经达到了一个新的高度。” 瓦德富尔提到了8月初发生在德国萨克森州莱比锡/哈勒机场的无人机袭击未遂事件，并指责俄罗斯试图用一架携带炸药的无人机摧毁乌克兰货机。莱比锡机场惊现无人机炸弹 靠近乌克兰运输机To view this video please enable JavaScript, and consider upgrading to a web browser that supports HTML5 video 瓦德富尔外长还明确指出，侵略乌克兰战争的后果正波及全球。乌克兰粮食丰收，但由于俄罗斯袭击乌克兰港口，粮食无法运往世界其他地区。“因此，俄罗斯正在加剧全球的饥饿和苦难，”瓦德富尔说道。 这位德国外长呼吁立即停火——首先从黑海开始——以确保粮食供应。他还要求全面交换战俘，重返基于国际法的谈判，以实现和平。 他呼吁道： “让我们彻底摆脱这种破坏与暴力的恶性循环吧！” 乌战：拦截机如何廉价、有效击落无人机To view this video please enable JavaScript, and consider upgrading to a web browser that supports HTML5 video (路透社、德新社、法新社） DW中文有Instagram！欢迎搜寻dw.chinese，看更多深入浅出的图文与影音报道。 © 2026年德国之声版权声明：本文所有内容受到著作权法保护，如无德国之声特别授权，不得擅自使用。任何不当行为都将导致追偿，并受到刑事追究。

articles.title: 增长预期翻倍，德国经济走出困境了吗？
articles.url: https://www.dw.com/zh/增长预期翻倍，德国经济走出困境了吗？/a-79413288?maca=chi-rss-chi-all-1127-rdf
articles.excerpt: （德国之声中文网）德国五大经济研究机构9月24日发布的联合秋季报告，将今年德国国内生产总值（GDP）的增长预测上调至1.3%，将2027年增长预测上调至1.1%。今年4月经济学家和政府顾问们曾预计，2026年GDP仅增长0.6%，2027年增长0.9%。 哈勒经济研究所的经济预测主管霍尔特默勒（Oliver Holtemöller）表示，目前德国经济状况“并不像公众情绪反映得那么糟糕”，企业和消费者都需要增强信心。他在解释上调2026年和2027年经济增长预测时表示，“经济发展比预期的要好”。 经济学家们表示，今年上半年，出口和制造业产出都出现了出人意料的强劲增长。“主要推动力来自稳健的全球经济以及席卷全球的人工智能热潮。” 与此同时，德国政府通过举债融资扩大基础设施和国防投资的扩张性财政政策，也为经济复苏提供了支撑。 德国企业招新难：速配活动能否缓解？To view this video please enable JavaScript, and consider upgrading to a web browser that supports HTML5 video 复苏仍显疲弱 结构性难题待解 不过，霍尔特默勒也提到，德国目前的“增长势头并不强劲”。由于能源价格高企和结构性问题，经济复苏的基础较为薄弱。 各机构预计2028年经济增长率仅为0.4%。基尔世界经济研究所的库斯（Stefan Kooths）表示，当前的问题主要是结构性的，因此改革势在必行。 库斯批评道，政府不应该每个季度都推出改革方案，然后又撤销。他表示，当前德国政府不明朗的经济政策加剧了德国整体经济疲软的局面。 这份联合经济预测报告的标题是《经济复苏伴随结构性问题：财政政策误入歧途》。这一报告受德国联邦经济部委托，由慕尼黑Ifo经济研究所、柏林德国经济研究所（DIW）、埃森莱布尼茨经济研究所（RWI）、基尔世界经济研究所（IfW）以及哈勒经济研究所（IWH）联合编制。 德国面临两大挑战 霍尔特默勒表示，德国面临两大挑战，人口老龄化和能源成本上涨，如果政府不解决这些问题，情况不太可能好转。 许多经济学家担心，若缺乏可持续的结构性改革，那么通过新增债务支持基础设施和国防支出的做法，只会带来短暂的经济刺激效果。 霍尔特默勒指出，仅仅由于人口老龄化等人口结构因素，德国未来中长期的经济增速就将不可避免地放缓。 DW中文有Instagram！欢迎搜寻dw.chinese，看更多深入浅出的图文与影音报道。 © 2026年德国之声版权声明：本文所有内容受到著作权法保护，如无德国之声特别授权，不得擅自使用。任何不当行为都将导致追偿，并受到刑事追究。 德国总理访华归来激情演讲To view this video please enable JavaScript, and consider upgrading to a web browser that supports HTML5 video

articles.title: 张又侠被整肃后 习近平二十一大连任稳了？
articles.url: https://www.dw.com/zh/张又侠被整肃后-习近平二十一大连任稳了？/a-79411740?maca=chi-rss-chi-all-1127-rdf
articles.excerpt: （德国之声中文网）中共中央政治局近日决定将中央军事委员会副主席张又侠和中央军委委员、联合参谋部参谋长刘振立这两位高级将领开除党籍和军籍。 新加坡拉惹勒南国际研究院（S. Rajaratnam School of International Studies）的中国安全问题学者詹姆斯·查尔（James Char）表示，“可以预期，习近平将继续对中国军事事务行使决定性的控制和影响力，进而巩固他对党和国家的支配地位。因为谁控制了中国人民解放军，谁就控制了党。” 习近平在2022年中共20大上打破惯例寻求第三个任期时，得到了时任中央军委副主席的张又侠的支持。张又侠因此被视为习近平在军中最核心的“红二代”盟友与护航者。作为“回报”，当时已72岁的张又侠也得以打破中共高层“七上八下”（67岁及以下可以留任或晋升，68岁以上必须离任退休）的惯例，不仅留任中央政治局委员，还升任排名第一的中央军委副主席。 不过，习近平与张又侠的矛盾与权力斗争在二十大不久后就爆发并激化，并逐渐从隐性博弈最终走向白热化。其间，外界可以观察到的重大事件包括张又侠在军队装备发展部时期的旧部、前国防部长李尚福落马、涉及巨额采购腐败案的火箭军被清洗，以及之后由习近平亲自提拔的军中亲信中央军委副主席何卫东和中央军委委员苗华被扳倒。 张又侠显然在最后的较量中落败。今年1月24日，中国国防部宣布张又侠和军中另一名高级将领刘振立因涉嫌严重违纪违法被立案审查调查。 解放军“二把手”张又侠的跌落To view this video please enable JavaScript, and consider upgrading to a web browser that supports HTML5 video “为党和军队消除了重大政治隐患” 张又侠和刘振立9月21日被宣布开除党籍、军籍后，中共中央军委机关报《解放军报》23日发文称，对他们的严肃查处，“为党和军队消除了重大政治隐患”，坐实了外界对张又侠、刘振立对习近平最高权力构成了最直接的政治威胁的猜测。有时事评论员认为，这是对张又侠和刘振立对曾企图夺权的委婉说法。 《解放军报》文章还明确要求全军官兵”要坚决拥护党中央、中央军委决定，自觉在思想上政治上行动上同以习近平同志为核心的党中央保持高度一致，坚决听从党中央、中央军委和习主席指挥，统一思想认识，坚定信心决心，勠力奋斗攻坚，不断赢得强军兴军历史主动。“这侧面显示军中仍存在不安、不满、抵触、不服从等情况。 军队作战能力或受影响 大规模的整肃行动在军队中带来的动荡也可能影响军队作战能力。《解放军报》该文指张又侠、刘振立”与党离心离德“、”严重助长影响党对军队绝对领导、危害党的执政根基的政治和腐败问题”对军队政治建军、政治生态和战斗力建设造成极大破坏。 伦敦托尼·布莱尔全球变化研究所（Tony Blair Institute）中国问题分析师鲁比·奥斯曼（Ruby Osman）表示：“很难想象如此规模的动荡不会给更复杂的军事行动——包括应对台湾问题的突发事态——带来问题。”“但她继续指出，“显然，在习近平看来，为了实现长期的纪律严明和战备状态，这种短期的动荡是值得付出的代价。” 预计习近平二十一大将继续连任 张又侠、刘振立落马后，原本由7人组成的二十届中央军委如今只剩下习近平和张升民两人。新加坡的中国安全问题专家詹姆斯·查尔（James Char）预测，中央军委这个领导班子要等到2027年秋季中共二十一大时才会补齐。 外界普遍预计，习近平将在二十一大上确立其第四个五年任期。而这将加大对内部安全的需求。尽管通过长期的反腐败斗争以及对军队“离心”者的清洗，中共党内已无能实质性制衡或挑战习近平地位的派系或个人，但是，面对复杂的经济及地缘政治环境，绝对集权并不意味着完全消除了意外风险，而官场和军队中也仍可能存在“畏权而不服德”的现象。 DW中文有Instagram！欢迎搜寻dw.chinese，看更多深入浅出的图文与影音报道。 © 2026年德国之声版权声明：本文所有内容受到著作权法保护，如无德国之声特别授权，不得擅自使用。任何不当行为都将导致追偿，并受到刑事追究。

articles.title: 陷争议的德国科研“灯塔”：与中国合作时疏忽安全
articles.url: https://www.dw.com/zh/陷争议的德国科研-灯塔-：与中国合作时疏忽安全/a-79410367?maca=chi-rss-chi-all-1127-rdf
articles.excerpt: （德国之声中文网）德国联邦教育与研究部部长贝尔（Dorothee Bär）9月22日向联邦议院研究委员会通报了毕马威会计师事务所提交的报告。报告称，位于萨尔布吕肯的知名信息技术安全研究中心CISPA，“与来自中国的高风险个人和机构开展合作”时，未能充分保护数据安全和商业秘密。 与中国的合作“异常密切” 毕马威的此次审计于今年6月启动。德国《商报》当时报道称，CISPA与中国科学家开展合作，密切程度值得担忧，人工智能和网络安全等领域的敏感数据和技术可能已外泄至中国。 《商报》的报道称，自2017年以来，中国已经立法规定其公民在必要时必须与情报机构合作。在一个专注于信息安全、数据保护和人工智能的研究小组中，19名成员中有18名来自中国。另一个研究机器学习与数据保护交叉领域的研究小组，甚至全部由中国科研人员组成。 北京：反对先入为主和抹黑 中国驻德大使馆则对此回应称，与德国是“在遵守法律法规的前提下开展互利合作“，并表示坚决反对“在缺乏事实和确凿证据的情况下，将中国与此类指控牵连在一起，反对这种先入为主、政治操纵、有针对性地抹黑中国的做法”，并强调“国际交流与合作不应被政治化”。 CISPA中心的科研主任、创办人巴克斯（Michael Backes）在此前接受Table.Media采访时也曾表示，没有来自中国的资金流入该机构，也没有中国的联合资助项目。他们的合作仅限于个案，这类合作“一直以来都属于正常范围，且往往是各方所希望进行的”。 德国联邦教育与研究部部长贝尔（Dorothee Bär）说：“打个比方，信息安全研究中心的大门一直敞开着。”图像来源: Milena Radatz/STEINSIEK.CH/IMAGO 未证实也未排除数据泄露 在长达400页的最终报告中，审计人员得出结论：既不能证实也不能排除安全相关信息泄露的可能性。这份报告未予以公开，德国教研部长贝尔表示，该报告经法律审查后将被列为“机密级别”。 虽然审计未能得出明确结论，但安全相关信息发生泄露的可能性始终无法排除。贝尔部长说：“打个比方，信息安全研究中心的大门一直敞开着。” 贝尔表示，审计人员在报告中批评了CISPA研究中心在防止商业秘密外泄方面保障措施不足。管理层在出口管制、保密和科研安全方面未能充分履行其职责。 她宣布，她的部门将再次在该研究所的监事会中占有一席之地。目前，该报告正接受仔细评估，之后将采取进一步必要的措施。 CISPA中心的科研主任、创办人巴克斯此前已被停职，并在调查结束前一直处于停职状态。所有与中国的研究项目也被暂时叫停。 在专项审计结果公布后，巴克斯确定离职。德国政府方面宣布，巴克斯与CISPA已经达成共识，双方将终止合作关系。相关声明指出：“双方对这家国际化研究中心的未来发展方向存在分歧。” 德国的科研“灯塔” CISPA信息安全研究中心是一家公共研究机构。2019年成为德国著名科研联合会“亥姆霍兹联合会”(Helmholtz)的会员。CISPA不属于政府机构，也不是大学，而是一家非营利的研究机构，资金主要来自德国联邦政府和萨尔州政府拨款。 德国总理默茨曾同萨尔州州长2025年8月参观CISPA，当时，默茨形容它为“灯塔”，高度肯定该研究中心的科研地位。 （德新社，商报等） DW中文有Instagram！欢迎搜寻dw.chinese，看更多深入浅出的图文与影音报道。 © 2026年德国之声版权声明：本文所有内容受到著作权法保护，如无德国之声特别授权，不得擅自使用。任何不当行为都将导致追偿，并受到刑事追究。 欧洲努力建设“数字主权”To view this video please enable JavaScript, and consider upgrading to a web browser that supports HTML5 video

articles.title: 打破11年慣例 川普親迎習近平落地華府
articles.url: https://www.dw.com/zh/打破11年慣例-川普親迎習近平落地華府/a-79406317?maca=chi-rss-chi-all-1127-rdf
articles.excerpt: （德国之声中文网）中国国家主席习近平週三（9月23日）抵达华府，展开为期3天的访美行程。美国总统特朗普亲自前往马里兰州安德鲁联合基地（Joint Base Andrews），在100英尺的红地毯、军乐队与礼炮簇拥下迎接习近平。 在迎宾仪式上，特朗普夫妇与习近平夫妇握手、交谈数分钟并合影留念，一架B-1轰炸机也飞越基地上空致意。 据美媒C-SPAN报道，这是11年来首次有美国总统在安德鲁联合基地迎接外国领导人。上一次是在2015年，由时任总统奥巴马迎接教宗方济各。特朗普和夫人梅拉妮娅迎接习近平及其夫人彭丽媛到访华府。图像来源: Kevin Lamarque/REUTERS 抵达华府后，习近平发表书面谈话，强调中美“应该成为伙伴而不是对手。” 他指出，中美双方利益“深度交融”，应推动“合作为主、竞争有度”的稳定关系。他也呼应特朗普的政治口号表示：“实现中华民族伟大复兴和让美国再次伟大，完全可以并行不悖、相互成就、造福世界。” 习近平表示，他期待与特朗普就中美关系、世界局势等重大议题交换意见，“相信在双方共同努力下，这次访问一定会取得丰硕成果”。 此次访问是习近平应特朗普邀请，继今年5月后，两人再次会面。根据白宫公布的行程，习近平24日将在白宫与特朗普会谈，并与企业领袖共进国宴、出席白宫军事仪式，25日则将参访收藏美国《独立宣言》和《宪法》原件的国家档案馆等。 贸易休战延至明年1月 美国财政部长贝森特週三表示，美中已同意延长贸易休战协议。 在与中国国务院副总理何立峰会面后，贝森特向《福斯新闻》表示：“原定11月10日结束的两国经济缓和期，将延长至1月10日，让我们有更多时间看看在经济方面能做些什么。” 去年4月，美国分阶段提高中国进口商品关税，最高达145%；中国则祭出反制关税，最高达125%，并限制部分材料出口。此后，美中多次同意暂停实施新关税、每次为期90天。 美中元首去年10月在韩国釜山举行峰会，达成更广泛的贸易休兵，内容包括暂停高额关税、稀土限制，以及对中国制造或中国拥有的船舶停靠美国港口所收取的高额费用。 此次延长贸易休战将确保双方关系稳定至2027年，但未达部分美国官员先前提出的延长3至6个月目标。 《彭博》引述华府智库战略暨国际研究中心（CSIS）专家甘思德（Scott Kennedy）指出，较短的延长期限显示，美国对中国在稀土及可能其他议题上的提议仍未感到满意，“这为峰会可能取得的成果设定了最低基准，市场可以据此开始定价，同时也保留特朗普与习近平亲自达成更长期协议的可能性。” 双方各自带著哪些“期待”？ 美中紧张关系不仅限于关税。中国也抗议美国对半导体及人工智能芯片实施出口管制，认为相关措施阻碍中国企业取得先进技术；美国则指控中国蓄意扣留部分关键原物料。 这场峰会登场之际，特朗普在国内面臨民意压力。舆论关注他如何应对伊朗战争，加上11月中期选举将至，特朗普可能在峰会中寻求短期可见的成果，包括争取来自中国的贸易订单。 中方则可能更著重长期利益，例如避免扩大美方对中国的高科技管制、延缓对台军售、限制台美互动等。 路透社引述分析人士表示，两国领导人可能都不认为自己有必要妥协。 战略暨国际研究中心中国问题专家卡根（Edgard Kagan）表示：“总统非常相信，随著时间推移，美国经济将持续成长，美国会变得更强大......当习近平与特朗普坐下来会谈时，习近平非常相信美国正快速衰落，而时间站在中国这一边。” DW中文有Instagram！欢迎搜寻dw.chinese，看更多深入浅出的图文与影音报道。 © 2026年德国之声版权声明：本文所有内容受到著作权法保护，如无德国之声特别授权，不得擅自使用。任何不当行为都将导致追偿，并受到刑事追究。

articles.title: 德语媒体：莫把AI比核弹
articles.excerpt: 德语媒体：莫把AI比核弹图像来源: DW（德国之声中文网）有人将中美人工智能对话同美俄之间的核武谈判相提并论。《法兰克福汇报》评论认为，这种比喻看似合理，实则荒谬。因为管控核武器的历来只有国家领导人，而人工智能的风险却来自大大小小的高科技企业，这恰恰就是人工智能带来的挑战。这篇题为《莫把AI比核弹》的评论写道： “前不久，人工智能企业Anthropic总裁阿莫代（Dario Amodei）有关中国的论述实在谈不上高明。他先是呼吁美国人工智能企业应当将对中国的领先优势扩大至三到五年。而接下来笔锋一转又写道，要想管控全球人工智能发展速度，就离不开‘同中国的合作’。 阿莫代似乎完全没有考虑过，此番表述会在中国引发怎样的反响。他似乎也没有搞清楚，中国对美国的技术和地缘政治霸主地位已经构成了多么大的挑战。事实上，美国现在并没有限制中国发展人工智能的施压手段。相反，中国却可以借助稀土的垄断地位，阻止美国采取任何过激行动。 如果当今世界的阿莫代、阿尔特曼和马斯克们真的相信人工智能即将威胁人类生存的警告，他们就必须接受在人工智能领域同中国开展平等合作的现实。否则，中国不顾及美国的担忧也是完全可以理解的。而中美两国在地缘政治领域的激烈竞争，将会促使中国不加限制地推动人工智能的研发。至于美国总统特朗普对全球共同管控人工智能风险持怀疑态度，倒也无关紧要。毕竟这位总统的立场说变就变，而且公开表达怀疑态度对日后的谈判也将有所帮助。试想，如果特朗普从一开始就对共同管控表示支持，他也就没有了讨价还价的筹码，而中国方面就会以同意合作为诱饵，要求美国做出各种让步。” 《法兰克福汇报》的评论指出，特朗普此前的表态恐怕只是他的“交易艺术”而已。因为没有特朗普的批准，中美本周开始的人工智能对话也就无从谈起： “将AI合作同美俄核武协定相提并论，看似合理，实则荒谬。因为管控人工智能风险的最大挑战，并不是地缘政治层面上能否开展合作。对中国党和国家领导人习近平来说，稳定和控制高于一切。他的情报部门刚刚将人工智能定性为政权的威胁。如果能同美国签署协议，减少无所不能的AI对共产党的威胁，那习近平又何乐而不为呢。当然，这种合作必须以平等为前提，因为在习近平看来，技术上落后于美国同样也是对其政权的威胁。法兰克福汇报：相较于美国，大规模中国AI企业的规模都较小。图像来源: Hector Retamal/AFP 有鉴于此，更大的挑战在于，如何将地缘政治层面达成的协定转化成各自国家的运作机制，从而有效地控制企业研发人工智能的进度。在美国， Anthropic, Open AI, Meta和Alphabet等科技巨头之间存在着激烈的竞争关系，每个公司都希望尽快推出更强模型，争夺客户，并让投资者对未来充满幻想。而管控机制就是为了防范企业为了赢得竞争去铤而走险。美国的资本主义之所以比欧洲更具活力，就是因为美国是以产品问责诉讼的形式来管控企业竞争的，但对人工智能来说，事后问责的模式显然极不适用。 中国的挑战则有所不同，除了阿里巴巴旗下的Qwen之外，其他人工智能企业规模都相对较小。Deepseek、Moonshot AI、Minimax 或Zhipu AI 都是一些初创企业。 例如，Moonshot只有大约三百员工。这类企业通常会以推出更强更新模型来显露头角，而提供优质服务则并非强项。他们能够失去的东西并不多，因此也就更具冒险精神。理论上，虽然中国的企业都处在北京的管控之下，但事实上，中国式资本主义往往比欧洲更野蛮激进，也更不受约束。 DeepSeek创始人梁文锋曾多次表示，他的目标是发展出通用人工智能，即所谓的超级智能。而阿里巴巴首席执行官吴泳铭也是类似的技术乐天派，他希望能够解除人类思考的苦恼。 这也正是人工智能和核弹的根本区别所在。因为，迄今为止，管控核弹风险的，从来都是国家首脑。 ” “欧中贸易正在进一步失衡” 《奥古斯堡汇报》评论认为，欧盟是时候就欧洲贸易失衡采取行动了，否则一切将为时过晚： “作为曾经的世界出口冠军，德国对贸易失衡问题并不陌生。也正因为如此，德国非常担心欧盟反对不公平贸易行为的措施会引发中国的反制。但现在已经没有时间继续等待和观望了。 欧洲人目前所走的道路非常崎岖险恶。毕竟一场贸易战中不会有任何赢家，而俄乌战争以及能源价格上涨已经令欧洲各国不堪重负。但是，如果北京不肯就平衡竞争条件迈出第一步，布鲁塞尔就必须单方面采取行动。 尽快同更多国家签署自由贸易协定，尽快推动统一市场的整合。除此之外，在对待中国不公平竞争优势的问题上，欧洲应以其人之道还治其人之身。欧洲目前所缺乏的，就是团结一致的精神。然而，如果现在还不采取行动，那么一切都将为时过晚，局面也将无法收拾。” 摘编自其他媒体的内容，不代表德国之声的立场或观点。

articles.title: 中国欧盟商会：欧中贸易失衡不可持续
articles.url: https://www.dw.com/zh/中国欧盟商会：欧中贸易失衡不可持续/a-79376658?maca=chi-rss-chi-all-1127-rdf
articles.excerpt: （德国之声中文网）中国欧盟商会在其年度报告中指出，去年，中国实现了1.2万亿美元的巨额贸易顺差，在全球集装箱出口中所占份额高达37%。根据中国的数据，截至8月底，今年头8个月，欧盟对华贸易逆差达到2420亿欧元。 报告指出，虽然这种情况部分源于全球对中国产品的需求，但“很大程度上”也归因于中国制造业产能快速扩张与国内消费不足的结构性失衡。自新冠疫情结束以来，中国消费支出一直未能复苏。与此同时，工业生产却大幅增长。 中国欧盟商会主席彦辞(Jens Eskelund)周二指出，“目前的这一趋势不可持续。“他还补充说，“完全看不到任何迹象”表明这种巨大的贸易失衡会在中期内有所改变。中国欧盟商会代表着1600多家在华经营的欧洲企业。 欧盟：对中贸易逆差已达“临界点” 欧盟也对与中国之间巨大的贸易逆差日益担忧。布鲁塞尔方面认为，中国巨额贸易顺差部分归因于中国方面的不公平做法，例如政府补贴和人为低估人民币。欧委会主席冯德莱恩上周表示，欧盟对中贸易逆差每天高达10亿欧元，已达到“临界点”，她将动用“一切可用手段”来减少对华“不可持续”的贸易逆差。 德国外交部长瓦德富尔本周一与中国外长王毅通电话。据德国外交部称，经贸关系是双方讨论的议题之一。德国外交部在推特上表示：“贸易关系必须建立在公平规则和真正平等的竞争条件之上。” 据中国官媒新华社报道，王毅表示，中欧不应打贸易战，”希望德国保持理性、务实态度，在欧盟内发挥积极作用，推动欧盟坚持自由贸易，摒弃保护主义”。 目前，欧委会已接连推出对小包裹征税、将钢铁进口基础关税从25%大幅上调至50%等多项限制举措。 10月8日至9日，中欧高级贸易代表将在北京举行下一轮经贸磋商。9月17日，中国商务部部长王文涛与欧委会贸易和经济安全委员谢夫乔维奇就中欧经贸问题举行了视频会谈。 延伸阅读：调查：德国企业希望欧盟对华采取更强硬政策 （法新社等） DW中文有Instagram！欢迎搜寻dw.chinese，看更多深入浅出的图文与影音报道。 © 2026年德国之声版权声明：本文所有内容受到著作权法保护，如无德国之声特别授权，不得擅自使用。任何不当行为都将导致追偿，并受到刑事追究。

articles.title: 德语媒体：人民币为何难以走向世界？
